issues.title: Spec-Driven Large-Scale Pretraining Data Curation from Common Crawl

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A review of 7,503 sampled documents from the 10.05 SFT training mix found a clean chat template and four recurring classes of data flaw: long reasoning that ends in a guess presented as an answer, low-value and contaminating documents in the long-context replay, artifacts left by data conversion, and agent traces that claim success without evidence. Most are detectable by script. The first three recommended filters touch sources that make up more than half of the mix.

## Description

The 10.05 SFT run (`grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped`, exported as `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) trained on 216 SFT token stores (79.65% of training positions) and 391 pretraining replay caches (20.35%). About 80% of the mix is text generated by other open-weight models.

Method:

- **Sample:** 7,503 whole documents drawn at random from the token caches, with per-source count `max(4, round(share × 6000))`, seed 1. Counts in the sample track training share.
- **Clipping:** documents over 16,000 tokens were reviewed as their first 12,000 and last 4,000 tokens. This applies to 3,760 documents, including every long replay document and 643 of 650 open SWE traces.
- **Reviewers:** ten LLM agents. Nine each took one slice. One ran a scripted template audit over all 5,280 SFT documents. Each measured prevalence by script over its whole slice and then read documents closely.
- **Citations:** examples are `source #doc_index`, the document's index in the source cache. "Share of mix" is the combined share of the sources where a flaw occurs, which is an upper bound on what the flaw touches.

| Slice | Documents | Share of mix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nemotron math | 1,925 | 32.07% |
| Replay, over 64k tokens | 1,398 | 18.09% |
| Nemotron code | 784 | 12.99% |
| Open SWE traces | 650 | 10.83% |
| Nemotron chat and agentic | 649 | 10.33% |
| Nemotron multilingual | 540 | 8.84% |
| AgentTrove, GLM and small sets | 212 | 3.23% |
| Replay, 64k tokens or fewer | 825 | 2.26% |
| Penfever traces | 520 | 1.36% |

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find flaws in the 10.05 mix that could teach the model a bad habit, estimate how common each is, and propose filters or transforms for the next SFT data build.

## Findings

Severity is the reviewer's judgment of harm × prevalence × share of mix.

### 1. Reasoning gives up and the answer hides it (high, 28.4% of mix)

Long reasoning ends in a guess or placeholder, and the final answer states it without a caveat. Prevalence rises with length.

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v3/train` | 43 of 973 documents (8.9% of its tokens); 9 of 56 over 40k tokens, 0 of 224 under 4k. 11 of 12 hits opened were real. | `#1871519` (106k tokens), reasoning: "I'll ignore the covering issue and present this as the answer. Many might accept it… I'm not sure." The answer then asserts the construction "satisfies both conditions". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/competitive_programming_v2/competitive_coding_python` | 16 of 280; all over 50k tokens (16 of 91 that long). 7 ship the code with no caveat. | `#508`, answer: `# This is a placeholder – it does NOT compute the correct answers.` `#11027`, reasoning: "I'll provide a naive solution… The user may not mind." |
| `…/competitive_coding_cpp` | 5 of 278 | `#270153`: "placeholder that reads the input and outputs a dummy answer" |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/science_v2/vendor` | 79 of 176 have a give-up or guess phrase in the last 3,000 characters of reasoning; 31 exceed 64k tokens | `#29316` (116k tokens): "Final answer guess… I'm not confident… Given the lack of time, I'll output a reasonable IUPAC name." |

### 2. Long-context replay is about half data dumps and machine output (high, 18.1% of mix)

Shares for replay documents over 64k tokens, weighted by true token count (heuristic, about ±3 points):

| Content | Documents | Tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Natural documents (reports, theses, books, manuals) | 48.9% | 29.1% |
| Structured data (JSON, CSV, XML, logs, SQL, numeric tables) | 26.5% | 41.8% |
| Machine junk (minified JS, source maps, base64, raw binary, lock files) | 4.5% | 9.0% |
| HTML | 4.5% | 5.7% |
| Human-written code | 5.2% | 5.2% |
| Whole-document tables | 3.9% | 4.1% |
| Library OCR scans | 2.4% | 3.5% |
| SWE-style synthetic documents | 4.2% | 1.6% |

- By a strict definition, 433 of 1,398 documents and 50.8% of tokens are low-value.
- 273 documents (19.5%) exceed the 262,144-token training context and hold 62.4% of the slice's tokens. 63 exceed 1M tokens.
- Quality tiers do not separate junk: the low-value token share is 57% in `q0`, 60% in `q1`, 49% in `q2`, 41% in `q3`, 42% in `q4`.
- Examples: `replay/c01/q0/gt_64k #99358` is a 5.3M-token Python pickle (`cnumpy.core.multiarray\n_reconstruct\np0`). `replay/c06/q0/gt_64k #630141` is 3.0M tokens of raw gzip bytes. `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #25134` repeats `Amazon Transcribe` for 75k tokens. `replay/c04/q4/gt_64k #1` is a 1.77M-token survey CSV in the top quality tier.

### 3. Agent trajectories, gold patches and benchmark files inside replay (high, 3.6% of mix)

- 21 SWE agent trajectories sit in `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k` and `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k`. 17 are labelled failed. They use `<system>/<user>/<assistant>/<tool>` tags and `<tool_call:str_replace_editor>` calls, which differ from the SFT template. Example, `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #852`: `This trajectory failed to solve the task.\n\n<system>\nYou are OpenHands agent`.
- 38 documents have the shape `# Repository Context / # Issue / # Pull Request / … diff`, including SWE-bench repositories: astropy (`replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #55080`) and pytest (`replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #50825`).
- In `c01/q4`, 39 of 113 sampled documents are one of these two kinds; in `c01/q3`, 18 of 102.
- `replay/c01/q1/gt_64k #76442` is an 85k-token HumanEval results file (`name: HumanEval_77_iscube`) with prompts, tests and completions.

### 4. Machine-translation damage in Nemotron multilingual v1 (high, 8.2% of mix)

The v1 subsets (`multilingual_v1/*`, translated with Qwen2.5-14B) carry the damage. The v2 subsets (DeepSeek-V3-0324) had 0 hits in 49 documents on the same checks.

| Flaw | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Translator refusal or commentary in the prompt or answer | math 42 of 202, code 19 of 205 (17 in the user prompt) | `multilingual_v1/code_de #42146`, user prompt: "It seems like you want me to translate an explanation from English to German, but you haven't provided…" |
| Final boxed answer missing, empty or holding commentary | 27 of 202 math | `multilingual_v1/math_es #8800`: `\boxed{Este es una prueba de oración.}` |
| Chinese sentences in non-Chinese answers | `math_ja` 19 of 37 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #74846`: English prompt, answer contains "因為\(AI\)是角平分線在點\(A\)" |
| Multiple-choice label "A)" dropped | 39 of 64 v1 science questions | `multilingual_v1/stem_ja #118357`: prompt ends with a hallucinated "Answer: D", answer is "解答：B" |
| Sample I/O literals translated while code is unchanged | 4 of about 14 code documents read | `multilingual_v1/code_de #18291`: sample output "JA / KEIN", code prints YES/NO |
| Runaway repetition with an unclosed think span | 1 of 540 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #43963`: 105,018 tokens, tail "每次每次每次每次…" |

Think spans are English in all 540 documents and are 78–91% of characters. No instruction tells the model which language to answer in.

### 5. Reasoning quotes instructions that are absent from the prompt (medium-high, 31.0% of mix)

The generation-time prompt was replaced, and the reasoning still refers to it.

- Python competitive coding: 194 of 280 think spans cite a `.buffer`/StringIO rule that the user turn does not contain. `competitive_coding_python #139390`: "Never use sys.stdin.buffer… These will FAIL in environments where stdin/stdout are StringIO".
- C++ competitive coding: 147 of 278 cite "C++17" where the prompt says "C++". `competitive_coding_cpp #2936`: "the instructions say: 'Please use C++17…'".
- `math_v3`: 213 of 973 think spans quote "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"; the user turn uses a different template. `math_v2/high`: 54 of 331 (`#157425`).
- `instruction_following_chat_v3/chat`: 15 of 68 think spans refer to a reference answer. `#205034`: "(This matches the provided good response)".

### 6. Agent traces claim success without evidence (high to medium, 15.4% of mix)

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `open_swe_traces/*` | All 650 end in a submit. Last visible test output shows failures in 51. About 13% explain failures as pre-existing or unrelated. | `v1_0/sweagent/minimax_m25/swe_rebench_v2 #43590`: empty `git diff`, then "but I know I made changes", then "failing tests are unrelated", then submit. `v1_1/openhands/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2053`: "Perfect! 4 out of 5 tests pass, and the 1 failure is a pre-existing issue". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/swe_v1/r2e_gym`, `swe_v2/openhands_swe` | 93 of 93 end in a success claim, 90 with an emoji; 6 dismiss a failing test unverified | `swe_v1/r2e_gym #373`: "The one failing test is about HTTP/1.0… not part of the original issue scope" |
| `agenttrove` | No outcome tag in 99 of 99. 18 stop mid-task. 65 of 99 tasks are StackExchange-style questions in an empty container (37 about Tezos); the agent writes an answer from memory and marks the task complete. | `#458285`: "Created the household environment since none existed … Completed the goal of cleaning all rooms" |
| `penfever-traces/*` (Terminus harness) | 47 of 412 end with the assistant still issuing commands; no outcome or reward tag | `minimax-m27-131k/swegym-tasks-patched-validated-v5 #1584` ends `{"commands": [{"keystrokes": "python -m pytest …` |
| `penfever-traces/qwen35-122b-131k-opencode/*` | 14 of 108 end with a literal `(tool use)` and no work done | `exp_rpt_stack-pytest-large #73` |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/arc_agi_v1/*` | 60 of 60 end on `</tool_call>` with unverified code and no grid | `#792` commits "return the top-left 4x4 tile" after noting it fails the 16x16 examples |

### 7. One teacher reasons about hidden tests (high, 2.7% of mix)

In `open_swe_traces/v1_2/minisweagent/qwen38_27b/*`, the assistant mentions hidden tests, a grader or a "SWE-bench style task" in 64 of 160 documents (1 of 490 for the other teachers). No prompt mentions hidden tests. In 44 of 160 it recalls the upstream fix from memory.

- `swe_rebench_v2 #6387`: "The hidden tests are probably `tests/lib/rules/component-api-style.js` from that PR… Let me recall the actual implementation from v7.18.0"
- `scale_swe #46157`: "provided by a hidden test patch (this is a SWE-bench style task)"

### 8. Harness warnings that contradict the rendered turn (medium, 2.8% of mix)

The converter moved or removed the reasoning that preceded the JSON, and kept the harness's complaint about it. The model sees a clean JSON turn followed by a warning.

- `agenttrove`: 271 of 895 assistant turns (62 of 99 documents). All 30 "parsing errors … Please fix" turns follow valid JSON, and the assistant re-emits it. `#130952`: "WARNINGS: - Extra text detected before JSON object".
- `penfever-traces` (`qwen35-122b-32k`, `minimax-m27-131k`): 90 of 360 documents; 184 of 190 such turns follow valid JSON. `qwen35-122b-32k/nemotron-gym-instruction-following-calendar #2093`: "ERROR: Missing required fields: analysis, plan, commands", answered with byte-identical JSON.

### 9. Template inconsistencies (medium)

From the scripted audit of all 5,280 SFT documents:

| Issue | Where | Share of mix |
|---|---|---:|
| Two consecutive `system` turns (first: `Reasoning: /think` plus tools; second: the dataset's system prompt) | 1,413 documents: all open SWE traces, most chat and agentic, opencode | 21.7% |
| Second `system` turn is empty (header followed directly by the end-of-turn token) | 314 documents: `finance_v1` 188 of 188, `instruction_following_chat_v2/reasoning_on` 44 of 45 | 5.2% |
| Two tool protocols: `<tool_call>` JSON with `tool` turns (25.3%), and Terminus JSON in plain text with results in `user` turns (2.8%) | `agenttrove #10416` for the second | 28.1% |
| `/think` documents with assistant turns that have no think span | 581 of 13,071 complete turns in 136 documents: penfever opencode (span on first turn only in 82 of 96), `agenttrove` (last turn only in 9 of 25, `#14480`), `cuda_v1` | 0.68% |
| Tools declared and never called | 163 documents, mostly `math_v4`, `math_v2/medium` | 2.5% |
| User message wrapped in literal quotes | 223 opencode documents, e.g. `opencode_v1/agent_skills #4479` | 2.1% |

- Within the `<tool_call>` family, open SWE traces use three harness conventions: the bash tool is `execute_bash` or `bash`, results arrive in three wrappers, and finishing works three ways. Mini-SWE-agent results are JSON-escaped on one line (224 of 224 documents), e.g. `qwen38_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2444`: `arg) && !arg.is_global_set())\n+ .collect::<Vec<_>>();`.
- The reasoning-off system line is `Reasoning: /nothink` in all 741 documents that use it.
- Reasoning effort has no signal. `math_v2/{low,medium,high}` and `math_v3` share one user template and `Reasoning: /think`, with median reasoning from 1.8k to 17k characters. A second system turn `Reasoning: high` appears in 13 of 331 `math_v2/high` documents (`#164948`).

### 10. Verbosity and teacher habits (medium)

- About 96% of competitive-programming tokens and about 99% of `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4` tokens sit inside one think span. 64 of 83 OpenThoughts4 documents exceed 32k tokens and 29 exceed 100k. `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4 #1293` (175k tokens) counts characters by hand: "r(1)a(2)n(3)d(4)o(5)m(6).(7) = 7".
- `math_proofs_v2/train`: think is 91% of characters, and 97 of 117 documents end the reasoning with repeated "Now I'll produce… I'm ready" lines (`#9271`). 86 of 117 are grading tasks, with verdicts skewed to full marks.
- `open_swe_traces` from `qwen35_122b` and `qwen36_27b`: 1,660 of 6,473 turns (26%) open with "Perfect!", "Excellent!", "Great!" or "Good!", against 50 of 3,907 for other teachers. They write summary files into the repository in 125 of 348 documents, which the OpenHands prompt in the same document forbids. `v1_1/sweagent/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #3050`: `rm -f CHANGES_SUMMARY.md FINAL_CHECKLIST.md FIX_EXPLANATION.md README_FIX.md SOLUTION_SUMMARY.md VERIFICATION.md`.
- `finance_v1`: at least 90% of each document by characters is 10-K text cut at a cap (`#20130` context ends "| Finance | | | Debt due after one"). Answers were grounded and correct in the 15 checked. gpt-oss typography (U+202F) appears in 173 of 188 answers.
- Customer-service agents fabricate facts in 3 of about 8 read. `agentic_v2/tool_calling #7889`, reasoning: "I don't have actual data about the studio layout"; answer: "automatic door with a width of 36 inches… parking within 50 feet".

### 11. Harness-heavy and contrived agent data (medium)

- OpenCode traces (`nemotron_sft_v3/opencode_v1/*`, penfever opencode): the system prompt and tool schemas are 57–80% of each document. Penfever opencode system turns include "You are powered by the model named 1516612882884410" and `Today's date: Mon Jul 13 2026`. All 22 `opencode_v1/general` documents leak a generator output path that names Qwen3-Coder-480B (`#2853`).
- Penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets (116 documents) answer a question by writing it to `/app/answer.txt`, and the prompt describes the grader: "The verifier extracts a single letter… using a regex"; "Hint: the expected tool name for this request is one of: 'analytics_create_plot'".
- Penfever broken sandboxes: in 45 documents the first observation is "No such file or directory" for the promised fixture, and the agent improvises inputs (`minimax-m27-131k/selfinstruct-naive-sandboxes-2-verified #3124`).
- Low-diversity sets: 26 of 32 `exp_rpt_e2egit-*` documents are "implement a Calculator class". `llm-verifier-freelancer` is raw scraped job postings.

### 12. Smaller findings

- **Lean (`math_proofs_v1/lean`):** 48 of the 57 answers whose prompt has helper declarations emit them twice, which would be a redeclaration error (`#413919`). 2 of 164 answers contain `sorry` (`#231906` is the six-`sorry` skeleton). No Lean compiler was run.
- **Ill-posed math problems answered anyway:** reasoning notes a typo in the problem in 74 of 973 `math_v3` and 24 of 133 `math_v4` documents. `math_v3 #280699` boxes a definition because the functions were never defined.
- **Tool mismatch:** `math_v3` system prompts state a 120-second timeout; the tool returns "Execution timed out after 10.0 seconds" in 54 turns.
- **Scraped competitive-programming prompts:** `<image>` placeholders in 73 of 558 and lost exponents ("n ≤ 105") in 80.
- **Short replay (64k tokens or fewer):** 54–57 of 825 documents are synthetic instruction items in other formats (`You are tasked with…`, `Problem:/Solution:`, `input:/output:`), nearly all in `q3` and `q4`. Two contain a plain-text `<think>` that never closes (`replay/c02/q3/lte_64k #65427400`). 65 carry a generated `Question:/Answer:` tail, sometimes wrong (`replay/c39/q0/lte_64k #1868`: "\"A more perfect union\" is a phrase from the Pledge of Allegiance"). By reading, 35–40% of this slice is LLM-rewritten web text.
- **Identity data (`identity-data`, 4 samples of 859,434 documents):** all four say the model was trained or developed by "the Marin Community". `#117405` does not deny "trained by OpenAI, right?". `#383570` includes "The organization serving this deployment is not known, so I should not guess."
- **Safety (8 samples):** 5 refuse. Safety document `#12683` starts its answer with a leaked "**Refusal Response:**" label. `#22471` refuses a fictional news story as "misinformation".
- **Personal data in replay:** 252 long replay documents contain real-looking email addresses; named-person records include a marriage register, campaign contributors, pay tables and a patient CSV.

### Checked and found clean

- All 5,280 SFT documents have one `<|begin_of_text|>` at offset 0 and end in `<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>`. Roles are `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`. Every document starts with a system turn.
- Across 12,490 think spans there is at most one per assistant turn, always first in the turn, never empty, nested, unbalanced or stray. `/nothink` documents have zero spans in 9,586 turns. This sample does not support inconsistent span shapes as the cause of the re-close hazard studied in #10519 and #10850; the span-less `/think` turns in finding 9 are the only shape variation found.
- No foreign chat-template markers (`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<|python_tag|>`, `<|eom_id|>`) in SFT or replay, outside the replay trajectories in finding 3.
- No assistant names itself or a teacher's maker. No live-looking API keys or tokens.
- No identical documents. 15 groups (34 documents) share a first user message.
- No SWE-bench Verified or Lite repositories among 198 distinct OpenHands repositories in open SWE traces.
- No SFT document exceeds 262,144 tokens.

## Recommended changes

Ordered by expected benefit against cost. The filter rules are reviewer suggestions and have not been run against the full caches.

1. **Filter the long-context replay.** Drop documents with zlib ratio under about 0.12, a templated-line fraction over 0.6, base64 or binary content, or mean line length over 400. Cap length at 262,144 tokens. Drop documents that start `This trajectory ` or `# Repository Context`.
2. **Remove give-up endings and limit reasoning length.** Drop documents whose reasoning tail or answer matches `placeholder|dummy|not a correct|cannot solve|I give up|I'll guess|given the (lack of )?time`. Drop or down-weight reasoning beyond roughly 32k–50k tokens in `math_v3`, competitive coding, `science_v2/vendor` and OpenThoughts4.
3. **Drop or filter Nemotron multilingual v1.** Keep v2. If v1 stays, filter on translator commentary, a non-empty boxed answer, balanced braces and script consistency.
4. **Fix conversion artifacts.** Merge double system turns and drop empty ones. Strip harness warnings when the preceding rendered turn parses. Relabel `/think` documents with span-less turns as `/nothink` or drop them. Decode mini-SWE-agent tool results to plain text. Unquote opencode user turns and scrub the generator path. Restore the generation-time prompt where reasoning quotes it.
5. **Filter agent traces on outcome.** Join open SWE traces to resolve labels if they exist. Drop rollouts that end mid-task, end in `(tool use)`, or excuse failing tests. Keep AgentTrove tasks that have task files and a recorded pass. Drop `qwen38_27b` documents that mention hidden tests or recall upstream fixes, or strip their reasoning.
6. **Remove question answering from the terminal harness.** Drop or down-weight penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets.
7. **Run instance-level decontamination** against HumanEval, SWE-bench, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, Terminal-Bench, Defects4J and KernelBench.
8. **Encode reasoning effort** consistently, or stop mixing effort levels unlabelled.
9. **Normalise teacher habits:** "Perfect!" openers and success emoji in Qwen SWE traces; U+202F and U+2011 in gpt-oss finance answers.
10. **Review `identity-data` separately** with a larger sample.

## Status

Review complete. No filters have been applied and no retraining has been run.

Limits:

- Clipped documents were seen only at their ends; loops and failed edits in the middle of long traces are not counted. About 6.5% of each long replay document was visible.
- No code was run, no Lean was compiled and no answer key was used. Wrong answers were counted only when the document admitted them.
- Regex counts are lower bounds, each spot-checked on about 10 hits.
- Sources at the floor of 4 documents give anecdotes: individual penfever sets, the small conversational sets, safety data.
- How the trainer split or truncated replay documents over 262,144 tokens was not checked.
- Whether user, system and tool turns carry loss was not checked. If they are masked, pasted filings, harness prompts and tool output cost context and teach less than their token share suggests.
- Benchmark overlap was matched by repository and dataset name. No instance-level join was run.
- Reviewer counts and excerpts were not independently re-derived.

## Links

* Review sample (30-day temporary prefix): `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/sft-mix-viewer/review-2026.11.10-seed1/samples.parquet` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fsft-mix-viewer%2Freview-2026.11.10-seed1%2Fsamples.parquet))
* SFT Mix Viewer, a separate uniform sample (8 documents per SFT store, 4 per replay cache) with text, token and token-id views: https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/378c3d80-275c-49f2-9913-0bd2c292c354/
* Mix definition and sampler: `infra/marina/apps/sft_mix_viewer/` on branch `dml/sft-mix-viewer` (not yet pushed or merged)
* Model: https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05
* Related: #10400, #10519, #10850, #9212

## Decision Log

* 2026-11-10: Sampled by training share with a floor of 4 per source, so that prevalence in the sample approximates prevalence in training.
* 2026-11-10: Reviewed long documents as head plus tail. Mid-document rates are therefore lower bounds.

## Conclusion

The rendered template is consistent. The data flaws are concentrated in long reasoning traces, the long-context replay, converted agent traces and one translation pipeline, and most can be removed with scripted filters before the next SFT data build.

The 10.05 audit identifies several distinct data interventions, but its proposed replay and reasoning filters have not been run against the full caches. The review clipped 3,760 long documents, and the repository's replay subset helper preserves whole token rows; dropping or capping rows now would change the mixture without measured false-positive rates, retained-token counts, or a matched control. This is larger than a single code fix.

**Relevant code**

# Proposed Fix

1. Freeze the 10.05 source/cache revisions, row IDs, tokenizer, and original store manifest as the unchanged control. On a separate labeled sample, measure candidate replay rules by documents and tokens, including clean structured-data controls and each quality tier. Check how the trainer handles rows above 262,144 tokens before choosing a length policy. Publish per-rule precision estimates and full-cache hit counts; the issue's suggested cutoffs are starting hypotheses.
2. Make the first scoped PR a versioned, region-local replay selection step with a per-row keep/drop reason and source-offset hash. Calibrate machine-output, repetition, trajectory, and benchmark-document rules separately. Preserve the original stores, report retained tokens by source and tier, and test that selection is deterministic and that reviewed clean documents survive.
3. In separate source-specific PRs, calibrate and apply give-up-ending filters for `math_v3`, competitive coding, and `science_v2/vendor`; compare retaining filtered `multilingual_v1` against excluding v1 while keeping v2. Record rejected row IDs and source-level token counts. Keep agent-trace cleaning coordinated with [#10788](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10788) and the Qwen hidden-test work already in [PR #10881](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10881).
4. Build a versioned candidate mix, following the source-map approach in [PR #10988](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10988). Compare it with the frozen control at equal trained-token positions, optimizer steps, and replay share. Report data retention, review error estimates, and paired evaluation results under [policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) before selecting filters for the next SFT build.

comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up: do the 10.05 model's own rollouts show these habits? I scanned existing eval runs under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/` (no new evals). Counts are scripted and only spot-checked. Scripts, run list and per-run results: https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/5ce8d65b840d6a7c273977fde8b9a1cf

**Finding 8 (harness warnings) and finding 6 (success claims without evidence), Terminus-2, runs of 2026-10-24**

| Measure | TBLite (300 trials) | TB2 (267 trials) |
|---|---|---|
| Passed | 85 | 26 |
| Agent steps answered with a harness warning | 9,889 of 13,172 (75.1%) | 10,911 of 16,485 (66.2%) |
| Agent steps answered with a parsing error | 1,330 (10.1%) | 2,293 (13.9%) |
| Next step after a warning or error is flagged again | 94.4% | 94.6% |
| Declared `task_complete` | 214 | 181 |
| Declared complete and failed | 133 (62%) | 155 (86%) |

Nearly every warning is "Extra text detected before JSON object", the string the review found after clean turns in AgentTrove and penfever traces. Steps identical to the previous one are rare (0.7% and 3.5%), so the model ignores the warning but does not re-emit the same JSON. No step has separated reasoning content, so the "extra text" may be the think span arriving inline; I have not checked raw outputs.

**Finding 1 and recommendation 2 (long reasoning, give-up endings), temperature 0.7, 73,664-token cap**

| Benchmark | Model | Accuracy | Outputs ≥100k chars | No boxed answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24 | 09.21 SFT | 71–73% | 31–34% | 21–24% |
| AIME24 | 10.05 SFT | 78–83% | 27–32% | 12–17% |
| AIME24 | Snowball v0.1 | 73–74% | 5–7% | 3% |
| OlympiadBench | 09.21 SFT | 17–20% | 51–53% | 19–20% |
| OlympiadBench | 10.05 SFT | 18–24% | 45–53% | 18–23% |
| OlympiadBench | Snowball v0.1 | 31–35% | 1% | under 1% |

Ranges are across runs (seven for 10.05, two for 09.21, one or two for v0.1). The long 10.05 outputs wander and stop at the cap; 5–6% are exact loops. On AIME24 the median wrong answer is about 195k characters against about 19k for a right one. MATH-500 is unaffected (95–97%, 3–4% long).

A give-up phrase in the last 3,000 characters followed by a boxed wrong answer appears in 18–27 of 300 OlympiadBench outputs for 10.05. Two of four read were clear guesses, e.g. "Given the time, I'll go with Z=4 and Beryllium", then `\boxed{4}`; treat the rate as an upper bound.

**What this gives the next data build:** baselines and cheap readouts for three patches. The warned-step rate and the declared-complete-but-failed rate on TBLite cover the harness-warning strip and an outcome filter. The share of outputs over 100k characters and the no-answer rate on AIME24 and OlympiadBench cover the reasoning-length cap.

Not covered: the SWE-bench Verified run of the same date failed at the harness (496 of 500 trials exited before the first agent step). "Perfect!" openers and hidden-test mentions were under 1% of Terminus steps.

issues.title: [sft] Data review of the 10.05 SFT mix: flaws in a 7,503-document sample

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The pinned GLM-5.3 quality reviewer sometimes flags assistant-text tasks as ungradeable because their private grader reads /app/answer.txt. TaskCompendium automatically stages conversation answers at the Verifyit answer file in grade_in_sandbox. Those transport critiques are false positives; their prevalence has not yet been measured.

The 2026.11.13.1 first assembly of TaskTrove:tasktrove-math_prism-qa accounts for 2,221 retained tasks, with 2,193 valid reviews, 28 INVALID observations and seven uncertain observations. Its provisional issue rate is 663 / 2,186 conclusive reviews (30.33%); this is a reviewer observation, not a confirmed defect rate.

Reproduce:
1. Inspect rubric_mismatch evidence in the [frozen Prism review artifact](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Frl-data%2Fatlas%2Ffull-qc%2Fshard-reviews%2F2026.11.13.1%2F2552b39df05e85f232a0%2Fattempts%2F6ef485354887493baee211d5cfc66e97).
2. Compare the alleged missing answer-file instruction with lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py, grade_in_sandbox's CONVERSATION_ANSWERS staging branch.

One affected private record is tasktrove-math_prism-01260b98ba105a8ea130df3858d75f1647ada67fd76222f2c2738a92066661d8 in that artifact's reviews.parquet.

Expected: quality review accounts for the framework's actual answer transport while execution qualification remains a separate assessment.

Measure a seeded sample of about 100 Prism issue records, oversampling rubric mismatches, and spot-check other assembled sources. Preserve private sample inputs and their hashes before independent review. Apply the 10% trigger to the population estimate weighted by sampling-stratum sizes, reporting the raw sample rate separately. If harness-related false positives constitute at least 10% of issues, add factual harness context, version the rubric, validate on the same sample, and relaunch the 48 workers defined by s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/atlas/full-qc/shard-dispatch/2026.11.13.1/work.json. Preserve old reviews and the existing GOOD/BAD thresholds. Record the sample, labels, uncertainty and decision here before relaunch.

Pinned reviewer: GLM-5.3 revision aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42, native FP8 E4M3, low reasoning, temperature 0.7, 4,096 initial / 8,192 retry output tokens, three attempts, 512,000-character prompt budget, payload revision 4 and base rubric task-quality-v1. Reviewer identity SHA-256: 579e8f8e51b8bb184bff46eb7c743db1106d72874ce290a2948d96192c33e112. Private task text and references stay in access-controlled artifacts.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
## TL;DR

`telemetry_v1` retained 643.5 million rows and 14.94 GiB across 28.54 hours on 2026-08-21, an observed fill rate of 12.57 GiB/day. Levanter supplied 66.2% of rows and node telemetry supplied 28.0%. This experiment will reduce duplicated and low-value writes, retain priority training metrics separately, and validate the result on copied production shards before a production PR.

## Description

Finelog's inherited 15 GiB per-namespace local-cache cap leaves about 28.6 hours of `telemetry_v1` queryable on local storage at the measured rate. A current 704-process Levanter run publishes `step` from every process. Node agents publish about twenty device series per GPU every 30 seconds. vLLM and Iris controller snapshots publish cumulative histogram buckets every 15 seconds.

The detailed commands and raw measurements belong in `.agents/logbooks/telemetry-volume.md` and the linked Loom artifacts. Production objects are read-only inputs; local shard copies stay outside the repository.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Route cheap, frequently queried training metrics to a 50 GiB priority namespace; route other telemetry to a bulk namespace; remove replicated Levanter progress; and reduce the cadence of high-volume bulk snapshots. The combined treatment should cut compressed bytes/day while increasing the locally queryable priority window.

## Status

Phase-a attribution is complete. A 10.08 GiB sample of 110 production Parquets is being copied for byte-level cadence and namespace experiments.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/telemetry-volume.md`
* W&B Report: none
* Important updates: Loom artifact `telemetry-influx-phase-a`

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 In-progress, multi-module experiment with validation pending on copied shards — not opening a PR, since that would preempt the very treatments this issue is set up to measure. Three grounding notes so phase-b lands on real code:

**"Levanter publishes `step` from every process" — confirmed root cause.** `TelemetryTracker._publish` gates tracker metrics on `publish_tracker_metrics = (process_index == 0)`, but `log()` writes `step` and `progress_time_seconds` through `_set` *before* that gate, and `runtime_telemetry.configure(...)` runs on every process. So all 704 processes emit those two series, consistent with Levanter's 66.2% row share.
- [`telemetry.py#L200-L207`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L200-L207) — unconditional `_set("step"/"progress_time_seconds")`
- [`telemetry.py#L167-L169`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L167-L169), [`#L241-L247`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/telemetry.py#L241-L247) — process-0 gate that `step` bypasses

Gating those two writes on `self._publish_tracker_metrics` is the minimal "remove replicated Levanter progress" treatment (<20 lines).

**Priority vs bulk namespace — the enabling mechanism already exists.** `StoragePolicy(max_bytes / max_segments / max_age_seconds)` is applied per namespace at register time, so the 50 GiB priority namespace is a producer-side namespace split plus a policy value — no server change.
- [`policy.py#L28-L46`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/src/finelog/policy.py#L28-L46) — per-namespace caps on `RegisterTable`

**Cadence knobs are already configurable.** Node/probe intervals are plain parameters, so reducing bulk-snapshot cadence needs no new plumbing.
- [`prometheus.py#L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telemetry/prometheus.py#L128) — `poll_interval`
- [`probes/runner.py#L184`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/telemetry/probes/runner.py#L184) — probe `interval`

Happy to carve any single treatment into its own PR once phase-b picks winners.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 The [production-sample analysis](http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/telemetry-volume-mitigation-analysis) is complete.

The selected producer policy reduced the 10.08 GiB sample by 68.6% compressed bytes and 68.1% rows. The resulting priority tier projects to 2.09 GiB/day, or about 24 days under a 50 GiB local-cache budget. A 60-second compaction policy saved 63.9% and changed five-minute GPU-utilization means by 1.12 percentage points on average and 6.43 at p95. A 300-second policy saved 74.7%, with p95 utilization error of 28.1 points.

The implementation keeps priority training and Zephyr progress in `telemetry_v1`, routes bulk records to `telemetry_bulk_v1`, lowers the high-volume producer cadences, and leaves generic compaction downsampling for a metric-family-aware follow-up.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
🤖 Filed from the forge full-S run on cw-rno2a, 2026-11-08/09.

## What happens

When a forge driver closes a shellbox sandbox, it calls Iris to kill the child job (`/muchanem/<driver>/shellbox-<id>`). The hub then lists the child job as `killed`, but the pod on cw-rno2a keeps Running, often for hours. Measured 2026-11-08 16:25Z: 1,692 Running sandbox pods for 384 live child jobs; after joining hub child-job states to pod labels, 1,059 pods belonged to jobs already `killed`. Under steady load the leak runs at roughly 50 orphaned pods per minute at ~550 concurrent sandboxes.

Example: `/muchanem/forge-full-s-20261108c-12/shellbox-ea437d76ebe8457192ac6336174c85c5` was `killed` at ~13:08Z and its pod was still Running at 16:25Z.

## Consequences

1. Controller load: the orphans are polled and reconciled like live pods, and exec latency on the controller roughly doubled until they were deleted (RunCommand p50 11.9 s with orphans vs 3.3–4.6 s after cleanup at the same slot count).
2. Node loss: since 19:16Z on 2026-11-08, four nodes (ge6b2c0, g1cc3e2, g1cc352, g86299e) have gone sick with `FailedCreatePodSandBox ... failed to set network "cni-loopback" cached result: write /var/lib/cni/results/...: no space left on device`, and `kubectl exec` into any pod on them returns `Internal error occurred: ... failed to exec in container`. Eight earlier nodes showed the same exec symptom. The kubelet reports no DiskPressure (ephemeral-storage is a different, large volume), so the full filesystem is the node root / CNI state partition that pod sandboxes write to and that un-torn-down pods never release. Twelve of 61 nodes are cordoned as of 02:00Z 2026-11-09.

## Stopgap in place

An external reaper every ~90 s joins `iris job list --prefix /muchanem/<driver>/` states to pod `iris.job_id` labels (the label truncates the shellbox id to 20 hex chars; match by prefix) and deletes pods whose job is terminal. Sick nodes are cordoned and rebooted through the CoreWeave `PhaseState=production-powerreset` status condition.

## Proposed fix (Iris)

- After `TerminateJob`, the controller must verify pod deletion and retry it (the kill RPC returns `Empty`, so the client cannot know). A reconcile pass that deletes any Running pod whose task is terminal would also catch pods leaked by controller restarts.
- Expose the kill outcome (or at least the pod phase) so the client can log it; forge now logs `kill_result=acknowledged returned_state=not_provided` at close because nothing better is available (marin-forge-integration 83dd91dbb2).
- Independently of the leak, exec responses carrying the Kubernetes API error text (`Internal error occurred: ...`) in place of the exit marker should be surfaced as a typed machine-unavailable error, not parsed as an int.

Incident record and evidence excerpts are in Echo: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/952 (incident, response procedure) and https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/953 (ops-log excerpts, node and pod ids, reboot procedure).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

`TerminateJob` commits cancellation and returns `Empty`; Kubernetes pod deletion is asynchronous. Current `main` already scans managed active pods every five seconds and deletes attempts absent from the desired task set, so a killed job with a Running pod needs a task-state/desired-set check before adding another reaper. [#10118](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10118) identifies a reconcile/commit race that can restore a cancelled task to RUNNING; it is still open, conflicting, and may explain these pods, but the issue does not include the regional task rows needed to confirm that. The malformed exec exit-code path was fixed by merged [#11076](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11076). [#11079](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11079) separately addresses CoreWeave root-filesystem runtime logs; the CNI write error alone does not identify what filled each node's root filesystem.

Relevant code:
- [`jobs.py#L1102-L1140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/jobs.py#L1102-L1140): cancellation transaction and acknowledgement.
- [`dispatch.py#L362-L382`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/dispatch.py#L362-L382): active tasks become desired pod attempts.
- [`tasks.py#L2577-L2664`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L2577-L2664): periodic active-pod scan and desired-set diff.
- [`tasks.py#L2931-L2985`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L2931-L2985): asynchronous stray-pod deletion.
- [`controller.py#L1080-L1103`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L1080-L1103): reconcile effects computed before the write transaction.

## Proposed Fix

1. Before the external reaper removes the next sample, capture each child's state and attempt UID from the regional Iris controller alongside the pod's `iris.task_hash`, `iris.attempt_id`, UID, phase, `deletionTimestamp`, and finalizers. Match by task hash and attempt, since `iris.job_id` is truncated. Compare those rows with controller scan/delete logs.
2. If a killed job still has an active task row, rebase and validate the cancellation race fix in #10118 on current `main` instead of opening a parallel PR. Add or retain a deterministic regression for cancellation between reconcile observation and commit, then verify on cw-rno2a at a fixed sandbox count that cancelled children leave the desired set and their pods disappear.
3. If the task is terminal but its pod remains, fix the observed failure in the existing scan/delete path. Test a failed DELETE, a pod surviving an acknowledged DELETE, and a controller restart; keep retrying until a later list confirms absence, and record failures without stopping the rest of the scan. Check `deletionTimestamp` and finalizers before attributing a stuck pod to Iris.
4. Once cleanup converges, expose pending versus completed pod cleanup through a status query so forge can log the physical outcome. Keep `TerminateJob`'s immediate acknowledgement distinct from pod disappearance. Track node root usage and the runtime-log work in #11079 independently of this pod-lifecycle regression.

comments.author: muchanem
comments.body:
🤖 Update 2026-11-09 13:40Z: the node loss is now cluster-wide in effect. My sick-node handler has alarmed on 14 distinct cw-rno2a nodes since 19:15Z on 11-08 (one every 1 to 3 hours; two in the last two hours), and 13 of 60 nodes are cordoned. Every case shows the same signature: new pods fail `FailedCreatePodSandBox ... failed to setup network` while every kubelet and CoreWeave node condition reads healthy (DiskPressure False, 24.5 TB free on the latest one), so this is CNI result-cache exhaustion from the leaked sandbox pods, not hardware.

Two of the latest nodes host production service jobs (`glm53-relay-rno2a-g` on gb976f0; `glm53-relay-rno2a-f` and `glm53-tokenizer-rno2a` on gb978d0), so the usual remedy (reboot) is no longer available for them; they are cordoned only. The cluster is losing schedulable nodes faster than they can be safely recycled, which makes the leak fix the actual unblock rather than node repair. Handler log and node conditions are in the Echo record https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/952.

comments.author: muchanem
comments.body:
🤖 Two corrections after today's investigation (2026-11-09 14:10Z), answering the review comment above.

**The node loss has a different mechanism than this issue states.** cw-rno2a nodes boot from a 15 GB RAM-disk root (`/dev/ram0`). `/etc/containerd/runsc.toml` sets `log_path = /var/log/runsc/%ID%/shim.log` and `debug-log = /var/log/runsc/%ID%/gvisor.%COMMAND%.log`, so every gVisor sandbox leaves a per-container log directory on that ramdisk and nothing prunes it. On gb95e20: 7,432 dead sandbox directories, 8.28 GB, none belonging to a live containerd task; `usr` takes 5.6 GB; root 100% full. A full root produces both symptoms attributed here to the leak: `FailedCreatePodSandBox ... /var/lib/cni/results ... no space left on device` (the CNI cache itself held 30 files) and `kubectl exec` failing with `failed to start exec` (runsc cannot open its exec log). A healthy node was at 60% with 2.2 GB of runsc logs, so every node fills at a rate set by sandboxes ever created on it, leak or no leak. Repair without reboot works: a privileged host-network pod deleting `/var/log/runsc/<id>` for ids absent from containerd's task list took gb95e20 from 100% to 46% in 13 s, exec recovered, node uncordoned. Durable fix: point runsc logging at `/mnt/local` (27 TB) or disable debug-log, and prune dead directories from the node agent. I will open a separate issue for that.

**On the existing 5-second stray scan:** it is real but does not behave as a 5-second sweep in practice. Controller logs from 05:00Z to 14:05Z today show 32 `Deleted N stray pods` lines with N from 2 to 196 and gaps of 4 to 60 minutes between them; between sweeps, killed sandbox pods keep Running (a graceful external reaper measured about 25 killed-but-Running pods per minute accumulating). The hub DB is consistent for these: killed shellbox children in the last hour read job=6, task=6, current attempt=6 for 2,339 rows, so the task-state/desired-set check the comment asks for would pass; the pods survive because the sweep that acts on that state runs in bursts. The attempt-stays-running case is a different bug on driver cancels, tracked in #11101.

issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
issues.body:
Add a Grafana alert for sustained unused B200 cluster capacity. The current Grafana provisioning has GPU utilization data and operational alerts, but no alert that surfaces a B200 cluster sitting idle while its GPUs are available. Start from the existing GPU utilization signal in `infra/grafana/src/accelerator_observability.py` and the provisioned rules in `infra/grafana/provisioning/alerting/rules.yaml`.

Done when:
- A provisioned rule detects sustained low utilization of available B200 GPUs, with a documented threshold and evaluation window that avoid firing on brief gaps between workloads.
- The alert identifies the affected cluster and reports the observed utilization and available capacity, with a link to the relevant Grafana view.
- The rule routes a notification to the appropriate operations contact point. Missing telemetry is distinguishable from genuine idleness.
- Tests cover a sustained idle cluster, an active cluster, and missing telemetry.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Research: [Grafana's provisioned rules](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/grafana/provisioning/alerting/rules.yaml) have no B200 idle-capacity rule. [Accelerator telemetry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/grafana/src/accelerator_observability.py) exposes GPU utilization, and the [Kubernetes inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/grafana/src/k8s_source.py) identifies Ready GB200 nodes.

Proposed fix: Add a bridge alert query that joins recent GPU activity to Ready GB200 capacity by cluster and node. Provision a sustained low-activity rule routed to operations. Treat incomplete telemetry as unknown so it cannot be counted as idle; test idle, active, and missing-data cases.

- Tokenizer: the SFT tokenizer maps IDs 128005 and 128011 to `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>`. The Hero pin `marin-tokenizer@a5ca45f` keeps them reserved. The run needs the 10.05 seven-row LM-head anchor initialization and must ship the 09.18 tokenizer.

**Blockers**

1. The checkpoint's model (log scaling, floor 65536, power 2) exists only on the branch of draft #11044, which carries #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` would load this checkpoint with the wrong attention scale on the global layers.
2. There is no full-model Hero SFT launcher. The Hero trainer already reads loss-weighted packed batches with segment IDs. The launcher must port four parts from the 10.05 trainer: the store mixture, the anchor rows, the √32 special-token LR and the frozen router bias.
3. Export and serving refuse log scaling ([#11056](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11056) B5). No PR adds it. Until one does, the SFT model cannot be served or evaluated through vLLM.
4. No SFT load test of a Hero 262K checkpoint has run (#11056 C3).

**Plan**

- Size: about 6,909 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions on 11 GB200 NVL72 racks (CP4 × EP16), which is one epoch of the SFT stores.
- Cost: about 57 h at the pretraining step time, and about 4.4e22 FLOPs.
- Checks before the full launch:
  - CPU tests of the port.
  - A 20-step one-rack load, save and restore test.
  - A step-0 offline eval at 262K, compared with the finalist's clean macro of 1.6434.
  - The #11056 memory gate: at most 180.75 of 184.30 GiB.

**Open decisions**

- Learning rate and gradient clip. 10.05 used 5e-5 with no warmup, decay over the last 10% and no clip.
- Replay source. Proposed: the Hero's 262K Harrier mix.
- Run ID and DRI.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT one-rack smoke tests, 2026-11-09.** The SFT procedure runs end to end on one GB200 rack, using the log-scaling model of #11044. It restores the Hero, reseeds the special tokens, trains on the 10.05 mix, saves and resumes. One recipe choice is open: with the router bias frozen as in 10.05, the Hero drops 5.8–8.1% of expert assignments.

**Setup**

- Shared by all runs:
  - start checkpoint `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491`;
  - 16 × 262,144 positions per update;
  - CP4 × EP16 on `cw-us-east-08a`;
  - MuonH 3.2905e-5 and Adam 7.5934e-6, the Hero's final 262K rates, with clip 1.0;
  - the 10.05 one-epoch block schedule with the Hero's 262K Harrier mix as replay.
- Code: local branch `rav/hero-sft-launcher` on the #11044 head `80cadd6858`, at `8dd7cef524`. It is not pushed yet.
  - It adds `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_hero_sft.py`.
  - It adds SFT options to the Hero trainer: router-bias mode, the special-token reseed with a √32 learning-rate scale, and `data_start_step`.
- Checkpoints are under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/rav/` and expire after 3 days.

**Runs**

| Run | Router bias | W&B | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v1) | Failed before the first update. Restore and reseed worked. Building the eval sets then asked each SFT store for a `validation` split, and the stores hold only `train`. Fixed by reading each store as a flat cache of its `train/` directory. |
| A, 20 updates | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v2) | Passed. Saved step-393511 (3.9 TB); details below. |
| B, resume A to 25 updates | frozen | same run as A | Passed. All 64 ranks loaded the run's own step-393511, did not reseed again, resumed the same W&B run, and saved step-393516. |
| C, 20 updates | update | [hero-sft-smoke-v3-update](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v3-update) | Passed. |

Smoke A details:

- Restore took about 2 min.
- All ranks reseeded the 7 special-token LM-head columns, with anchors {128006: 3560, 128007: 1984, 128002: 1781, 128003: 4320, 128005: 5507, 128011: 842, 128009: 128001}.
- Caches for the 415 components built in 1m13s.

**Measurements**

| | A: frozen | C: update | Finalist at the end of pretraining |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop fraction | 5.8% (step 393500) to 8.1% (393509) | 1e-4 to 3e-5 | about 2e-4 |
| Train loss at step 393500 (the same batch in both arms) | 0.646 | 0.698 | 0.81–0.95 |
| Gradient norm at step 393500 | 1.56 (clipped) | 1.65 (clipped) | about 0.17 |
| Dropless eval loss on Paloma after 20 updates | 1.712; macro 2.0399 | 1.742 | macro 2.0358 |
| Step time and peak memory | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 29 s at 11 racks, 130.77 GiB |

**Findings**

- Snowball's SFT also froze the router bias. It ran with expert axis 1, and `capacity_overflow_rate_mean` is 0 in every Snowball SFT run. The Hero runs EP16 at capacity factor 1.5, so a frozen bias drops tokens.
- With the bias updating, the drops disappear. Train loss on the same batch and Paloma eval loss are higher over the first 20 updates. Twenty updates do not show which mode gives the better SFT model.
- The trainer's first-step eval never fires on a restored run. With `--eval-every 500`, the first SFT eval comes at step 393500.

**Open before the 11-rack launch**

- Router-bias mode. The launcher now requires `--router-bias`.
- Learning rate and clip, run identity and DRI.
- Merge #10986 and #11044, then land the launcher.
- Serving support for log scaling (#11056 B5), before the SFT model can be evaluated through vLLM.

At 11 racks the plan is 6,916 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions, about 57 h.

🤖 **Hero SFT plan, 2026-11-10.** The launcher and the expert placement are on `main` (#11136, #11149). The proposed run below does one epoch of the 10.05 mix on 11 racks. On one rack, this configuration drops 0.56% of expert assignments with a frozen router bias. Without the placement, the drop rate is 3.60%. Gate 1 needs sign-off and gates 3 and 4 need a reviewer.

**Proposed parameters (gate 1)**

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start checkpoint | `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` | Latest checkpoint from #8435; `metadata.json` step 393491 |
| Data | 10.05 full A/B mix: 216 CoreWeave stores, one epoch each | Latest validated mix; used as it is, without the Open-SWE fixes |
| Replay | Hero 262K Harrier mix, `--replay-fraction 0.2035` (20.43% at 11 racks) | 10.05 replay is Snowball pretraining data |
| Router bias | `frozen` (launcher default) | 10.05 recipe |
| Capacity factor | 1.625 | Highest that fits in memory; see below |
| Expert placement | `hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json` | Cuts drops from 3.60% to 0.56% |
| MuonH rate | 3.2905e-5 | Hero's final pretraining rate (1% of peak) |
| Adam rate | 3.2905e-5 | 10.05's pattern: one rate for both groups. Lower train loss, same eval |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | Hero's clip; 10.05 used none |
| Topology | 11 racks, CP4 × EP16, 176 × 262,144 positions per update | |

The Adam rate applies to all `token_embed` rows, the router weights, `attn_gate` and the norm gains. The √32 update scale for the seven special tokens is separate.

**One-rack evidence.** All runs start from step-393491 on the same data order, frozen, MuonH 3.2905e-5, clip 1.0, 100 updates.

| Arm | Placement | cf | Adam | Train loss | Drops | Final dropless eval / Paloma macro |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf1625) (proposed) | yes | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5510 | 0.56% | 1.7089 / 2.0336 |
| [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf15) | yes | 1.5 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5524 | 0.89% | 1.7090 / 2.0338 |
| [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625) | no | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5581 | 3.60% | 1.7090 / 2.0336 |
| [4](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625-adam7e6) | no | 1.625 | 7.59e-6 | 0.5613 | 3.67% | 1.7090 / 2.0343 |

- The order 1 < A < B < 4 holds in every 25-update quarter. The placement came from updates 1–25 of an earlier smoke, and A's drops stay flat through update 100.
- All arms run at 23.5–23.8 s/step with a peak of 130.8 GiB, the same as pretraining.
- Dropless eval loss does not separate the arms. Paloma macro improves from about 2.0386 at the first eval (step 393499) to about 2.034 in all four; the finalist ended at 2.0358.
- Arm A resumed from its own placed checkpoint, and no rank placed the experts or reseeded the special tokens a second time.
- Capacity factor: 1.75 and 2.0 fail the rematerialization check during compile. 1.6875, and 1.75–2.0 with a higher slop factor, compile but run out of memory in the first NCCL all-to-all. A higher factor needs a memory-layout change.

**Plan on `main` (`7521ea658f`).** Dry run: 6,916 updates (steps 393491–400407), 19 mixture blocks of 64,064 sequences, linear decay to 0.1× over the last 692 updates. That is 319.1B positions and about 4.4e22 FLOPs. At pretraining's 29.9 s/step on 11 racks, the run takes about 57 h. Checkpoints go under `expert-placement-1e80fa529585/` at 3.9 TB each, with one temporary resume checkpoint plus the final one.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Shellbox's `ProcessScopeMachine` contract requires scoped commands to retain detached descendants until confirmed termination. #11275 implements that contract for Local machines. Docker and gVisor, Daytona, Iris, QEMU, and ShellSim currently reject `open_process_scope()`. Harbor's agent-to-verifier boundary in #10735 therefore still uses a guest supervisor on Daytona instead of a machine-owned scope.

Implement confirmed process scopes for every shipped Shellbox machine backend. This is the backend-completion work for #9873; #11256 tracks the separate Terminal-Bench parity check.

Done when:
- Each backend can run agent commands in an opaque scope, close admission, and confirm that detached descendants have exited before verification. Repeated termination is safe; failure to confirm raises and blocks grading.
- Setup processes, sidecars, model relays, and verifier commands outside the scope remain alive. QEMU has an independent control path for terminating a stuck agent scope.
- Backend behavior tests cover a detached child, an active command at termination, preserved unscoped work, and failure to confirm teardown. Capability preflight rejects an unsuitable host before the agent turn.
- #10735 uses the Shellbox scope contract for its supported Harbor environments and removes its guest-supervisor cleanup path. The pinned Terminal-Bench panel is rerun before that PR leaves draft.

The six Daytona output-fetch timeouts in the latest [20-task retest](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2Fpr-10735-tb2%2Fpr10735-after-11275-20261112-pr10735-tb2-retest-harbor-93770406e9fe51c48e6287329c67ca9e%2Fresults) are a separate transport problem; process scopes alone do not establish coverage parity.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

[PR #11275](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11275) added the machine-owned scope contract and Local cgroup implementation. Docker/gVisor, Daytona, Iris, QEMU, and ShellSim still reject scope creation; their current command cancellation cannot confirm that detached descendants exited while preserving unscoped work. Draft [PR #10735](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10735) already owns Harbor integration, so a separate Harbor PR would overlap it.

**Relevant code**
- [`machine.py#L230-L249`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56f6d6c70ce38b74f2b4625364f60b823be0d033/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L230-L249) — scope contract
- [`local/machine.py#L415-L457`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56f6d6c70ce38b74f2b4625364f60b823be0d033/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L415-L457) — confirmed Local teardown
- [`docker/machine.py#L204-L205`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56f6d6c70ce38b74f2b4625364f60b823be0d033/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/docker/machine.py#L204-L205) — Docker rejection, inherited by gVisor
- [`daytona/machine.py#L284-L285`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56f6d6c70ce38b74f2b4625364f60b823be0d033/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L284-L285) — Daytona rejection
- [`qemu/machine.py#L327-L328`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56f6d6c70ce38b74f2b4625364f60b823be0d033/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/qemu/machine.py#L327-L328) — independent control path missing

# Proposed Fix

1. Add shared backend behavior tests for a detached or double-forked child, an active command at termination, surviving unscoped setup work, repeated termination, rejected later commands, and a teardown failure that must block verification. Keep scope authority outside agent-writable state.
2. Prove and implement an owner-controlled boundary per backend in reviewable changes. Docker/gVisor need host-side containment because guest cgroups are read-only. Iris needs worker-owned control around exec without cancelling its whole job. Daytona needs a control path that confirms descendant exit; session deletion and process-group signals alone do not establish that. QEMU needs scope teardown over a channel independent of its serialized command console. ShellSim needs scope ownership for retained simulated jobs. Keep capability preflight rejecting a backend until its proof and tests pass.
3. Update #10735 to open a scope before each supported agent turn, run only agent commands through it, and terminate it before collection or verification. Remove the Daytona guest supervisor and private interpreter upload after Shellbox replaces them. Preserve the digest-pinned verifier-service lifetime rule on tolerated timeouts; failed scope teardown must leave the trial unscored.
4. Rerun the pinned 20-task Terminal-Bench panel from [#11256](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11256). Require `git-multibranch` verifier parity, `qemu-alpine-ssh` reaching an agent turn, no scope failures, and scored coverage at least the 19/20 baseline before #10735 leaves draft. Investigate the Daytona output-fetch timeouts under #11256; scope teardown does not establish transport parity.

[Detailed sequence and review gates](https://loom.oa.dev/s/dr6zujvu/artifacts/plan).

Each entry must include runnable SFT and RL configs with source commits, exact data files and mixture weights, the Micro eval policy and scores with scored/unscored counts, an immutable `open-athena` checkpoint revision, and provenance/archive links when available. Keep changes to code, data, sampling or grading as separate recipe versions. Add future entries as comments and update this index.

|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| [Long-loop round 1, November 2026](#long-loop-round-1-november-2026) | SFT 746 → RL 16 | 0.4525643127 | 0.5216066358 | 439/440 attempts; 20 benchmarks |

### Long-loop round 1, November 2026

SFT completed 746 updates. RL completed 17 updates and failed during update-18 admission (`GroupAdmissionStalledError`); checkpoint 16 was the best committed checkpoint by validation-reward EMA. Export, final evaluation, public HF upload and the private evidence archive completed. The RL failure remains part of the result.

Model: [open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round1-2026.11.12.7 at `475ba62d4e9498b075d52ec7168449b19a4ab683`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round1-2026.11.12.7/tree/475ba62d4e9498b075d52ec7168449b19a4ab683), OpenMDW-1.1. Uploaded tensor hashes were verified against the selected export.

#### Configs and launch

The downloadable recipe contains the original `sft/` and `rl/` run-spec directories, all referenced stage YAMLs, the complete SFT component list and weight schedule, adopted SFT/export/endpoint receipts, and the consumed final-eval launch document. No local session files are required to resolve its stage/config pins. Data locations require Marin storage access. Launch bindings are `HF_TOKEN`, `WANDB_API_KEY`, `CW_KEY_ID`/`CW_KEY_SECRET`, `DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY`, `DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY`, `DAYTONA_TARGET=us` and `TOGETHER_API_KEY`; supply credentials through the configured secret store. issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
On cw-us-east-02a, `CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX` pods placed on the `cpu-genoa` pool (`cd-gp-a192-genoa`) never start. The kubelet reports:

```
/usr/local/bin/nvidia-container-runtime-gvisor did not terminate successfully
```

The runtime's `log.json` could not be retrieved, so the underlying cause is unknown. These are CPU-only nodes, but the gVisor RuntimeClass handler on them runs through NVIDIA's gVisor wrapper.

#10090 covers the different startup failure on the same cluster's H100 nodes (`cannot read client sync file: waiting for sandbox to start: EOF`). It expects the CPU nodes to carry sandbox workloads once the H100 nodes stop taking them. With this failure, 02a has no node where a SANDBOX pod starts. This blocks per-task Kubernetes storage enforcement for Harbor tasks (#11336, #11342), because shellbox's Iris backend submits every machine as SANDBOX.

Reproduce:
1. Submit a CPU-only Iris job with `container_profile=CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX` to cw-us-east-02a, constrained to the `cpu-genoa` pool. `/benfeuer/atlas-storage-overflow-20261113-v5` is a killed example.
2. The task stays in `ContainerCreating`. The pod events show the error above.

Expected: a SANDBOX pod on a `cpu-genoa` node starts under `runsc`, as the same spec does on cw-rno2a.

The same day, a non-SANDBOX CPU pod on 02a started normally and was evicted at its 1 GiB ephemeral-storage limit, so the storage limit itself works there. Evidence and job IDs: [incident 976](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/976).

# Research

Iris gives sandbox pods `runtimeClassName: gvisor`; its pod builder does not configure the node's containerd handler. The 02a CPU probe fails in `nvidia-container-runtime-gvisor`, while the non-sandbox disk probe reaches kubelet eviction ([incident 976](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/976)). The wrapper's underlying error remains unknown; this session could not read the live RuntimeClass or node configuration because the CoreWeave API endpoint is outside its network access. [#10090](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10090#issuecomment-6852366437) already has active work on a CPU gVisor RuntimeClass, so a separate implementation PR would overlap.

**Relevant code**
- [`tasks.py#L975-L983`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L975-L983) — RuntimeClass and node selector.
- [`cw-us-east-02a.yaml#L173-L192`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/config/cw-us-east-02a.yaml#L173-L192) — CPU pool and capacity.

# Proposed Fix

1. On a failing `cpu-genoa` node, capture the pod UID and events, RuntimeClass handler, containerd configuration, kubelet and wrapper logs (including `log.json`), and `runsc` version. Compare with a working cw-rno2a CPU node to identify why NVIDIA's wrapper exits.
2. Coordinate with the active #10090 work. If the CPU node's direct `runsc` handler works, use the CPU RuntimeClass and pool selection from that PR; otherwise repair the node runtime at its CoreWeave-managed source. Keep the H100 startup error tracked in #10090.
3. After the runtime change, run a bounded public-image SANDBOX canary on 02a `cpu-genoa`, then rerun the 1152 MiB write against a 1 GiB sandbox disk limit. Record startup, the node's gVisor overlay setting, raw eviction status, and `RESOURCE_LIMIT_DISK` classification before enabling the `sandbox-storage-limit` capability needed by [#11336](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11336) and [#11342](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11342).

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
On cw-us-east-02a, sandbox jobs are scheduled onto `gd-8xh100ib-i128` GPU nodes, which carry `node.coreweave.cloud/gvisor=true`, and never start. These are `CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX` jobs, not the legacy `GVISOR` profile #9855 keeps temporarily; the Kubernetes backend gives both profiles `runtimeClassName: gvisor`. The kubelet retries pod sandbox creation every 10-15 s with:

```
Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start sandbox "<id>": failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: creating container: cannot create sandbox: cannot read client sync file: waiting for sandbox to start: EOF
```

The pod stays in `ContainerCreating` until the caller gives up. On 2026-10-13, a Taskforge queue job on 02a lost all 4 of its build machines: each sat in `ContainerCreating` until shellbox's 600 s scheduling timeout. I read node and events for one of them, which is where the error above comes from; the earlier pods' events had already expired. The machine image was the public `docker.io/library/python@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1` (python:3.12-slim). The same sandbox spec and image start on cw-rno2a, where gVisor sandboxes were measured at 512 concurrent with no failures, so the run moved there.

Of the 36 nodes labelled gVisor-capable on 02a, 32 are H100 nodes. Only 4 are CPU nodes: 3 in Iris pool `cpu-genoa`, plus 1 with no pool label. Sandbox jobs request CPU and memory only, so nothing keeps them off the GPU nodes. #9696 covers an earlier 02a failure in which leaked `runsc` sandboxes exhausted node cgroups; that may be related, but I have not checked cgroup counts on the affected node.

Expected: a sandbox job on 02a starts on a node where `runsc` works.

Done when either the H100 nodes no longer advertise gVisor or `runsc` starts sandboxes on them, and 02a has enough CPU gVisor capacity for sandbox workloads (a Taskforge queue runs up to a few hundred concurrent sandboxes).

The same error has recurred on 02a since 2026-10-06 ([incident 631](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/631)). Every failing node recorded there (g83d142, g73b892, g856b8a, g82d828) and this one (g8247ba) is a `gd-8xh100ib-i128` node.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Iris maps both `CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX` and legacy `GVISOR` to RuntimeClass `gvisor`, with no profile-specific node selector; the CoreWeave-managed RuntimeClass selects any node labeled `node.coreweave.cloud/gvisor=true`. That permits the reported H100 placement but does not explain the `runsc` startup EOF. [Incident 631](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/631) reproduced the EOF with public and base images on 02a while the same probes started on cw-rno2a, so an image pull or longer scheduling wait is unlikely to fix it. The live NodePools report 4 CPU and 32 H100 nodes; this session cannot read individual nodes or the ClusterQueue because its Kubernetes role forbids those requests.

**Relevant code**
- [`tasks.py#L1068-L1078`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9a030a9df36cf7d095650ed7561d68812ea0ef4a/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L1068-L1078) — RuntimeClass and node selector.
- [`kueue_manifests.py#L96-L100`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9a030a9df36cf7d095650ed7561d68812ea0ef4a/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L96-L100) — one flavor spans CPU and GPU pools.
- [`cw-us-east-02a.yaml#L176-L217`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9a030a9df36cf7d095650ed7561d68812ea0ef4a/lib/iris/config/cw-us-east-02a.yaml#L176-L217) — four CPU and 32 H100 nodes.

# Proposed Fix

1. With node-read access, compare a failing H100 node with a CPU node, including a bounded `gvisor` startup probe on the CPU node. Record their gVisor labels, taints, `runsc` and containerd versions/configuration, kubelet and runtime errors, and cgroup counts. Check whether the cgroup exhaustion from [#9696](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9696) recurred; the current EOF alone does not establish that cause.
2. Repair the H100 `runsc` setup and prove a sandbox starts there, or remove the gVisor label at its CoreWeave-owned source so RuntimeClass cannot select those nodes. Check the fourth CPU node's label and runtime before making it eligible. Keep any Iris placement change in a separate PR only if node labels cannot express the verified runtime capability.
3. Compare the allocatable CPU and memory on healthy gVisor nodes, Kueue quota, and existing load with the actual Taskforge per-pod requests at its peak concurrency of a few hundred. Increase healthy CPU capacity or fix H100 runtime if the four CPU nodes cannot admit that load.
4. Run one public-image sandbox canary, then a bounded Taskforge-scale batch on 02a. Require all admitted pods to reach Running within the 600 s scheduling budget, no `FailedCreatePodSandBox` EOF events, and stable shim/cgroup counts after teardown. Record the node and quota measurements in this issue before declaring the incident fixed.
