issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Integrate the original 5,200-question [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) through **TaskCompendium** (PR #10984): six biological subtasks, one answer per question, no tools or retrieval. The PR targets `main` after evaluation migration #10957 merged and reuses its corpus pipeline. Reporting, public launcher access, and official-policy admission remain separate.

Decisions:

| Topic | Agreed approach and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Use pinned `HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa` binary-choice (BCQ) and multiple-choice (MCQ) data. All 5,200 evaluation rows match the author release. Exclude Carbon’s modified tasks and subsets. |
| Reporting | Foreground the six biological subtask scores and their overall mean. Within each subtask, average BCQ and MCQ equally; then average the six subtasks equally. This prevents the smaller motif task from being underweighted. Retain BCQ/MCQ summaries, all 12 cells, denominators, and ordinary correct counts. No chance correction. |
| Prompt | Use the fixed optimized prompt from the public runner. Optimization already happened offline; no new prompt search. Fetch the pinned prompt externally without executing upstream code or bundling the prompt in Marin. |
| Generation | Temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95, matching the released runner. Shared total cap of 16,384 generated tokens, including reasoning, visible analysis, and the answer. Enable thinking where supported; pin effort and verify token-budget semantics per provider. |
| Implementation | Reuse TaskCompendium acquisition, task conversion, source-grader packaging, and evaluation protocols. Retain the small GenomeQA parser, per-cell weights, and subtask/format groups. Add final-only response selection; do not add a custom runner or reducer. |
| Grading | Grade final content only. Reject ambiguous/invalid options; unparseable and length-truncated answers score zero. Transport failures remain ungraded. Retain the agreed parser; recovering observed formatting failures would add only 0.0167 percentage points. |
| Asset handling | Reuse licenses remain unspecified. Keep questions and responses in controlled storage, tests synthetic, and public reports aggregate-only. External fetching does not resolve use terms. |

Current validation (2026-11-13, 18:47 UTC): **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it thinking-off is complete: 5,200/5,200 graded, macro 44.08%, BCQ 54.43%, MCQ 33.73%. Thinking-on is partial: 3,368/5,200 graded; a continuation at concurrency 64 is queued but blocked by Iris federation.** Off-mode pooled accuracy is 41.79% (2,173 correct); 12 length truncations score zero, with no parsing failures or separately classified refusals. All 5,091 original successful off-mode responses and grades are unchanged. Usage is 7,298,523 input and 1,436,334 output tokens. No complete paired score is claimed.

| Biological subtask | Thinking-off macro |
| --- | ---: |
| Enhancer vs. promoter | 38.60% |
| Splice sites | 37.30% |
| Species classification | 47.10% |
| Histone marks | 40.70% |
| Transcription-factor binding sites | 41.80% |
| Motifs | 59.00% |

After the first recovery budget, the parent, broker, and serving worker were stopped before submitting `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-thinking-on-20261113`. The user approved up to four more hours on two H100s (eight H100-hours), ending about 20:58 UTC / 4:58 p.m. Eastern. It resumes only the 3,151 remaining thinking-on questions through native retry/resume. Hashes of all 2,049 completed on-mode answers are saved for preservation checks. The continuation uses a source snapshot at `fe813e34c2`, with the same model, protocol, seed, output cap, and concurrency; it does not adopt the PR's new main runtime mid-run.

Concurrency check: the private launcher initially overrode Marin’s native default of 64 with an unbenchmarked value of 32. After the user approved testing 64, `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-thinking-on-c64-20261113` was submitted for the remaining 1,832 questions, retaining the original 20:58 UTC deadline and two-H100 allocation. Model, prompts, sampling, token limits, and runtime revision are unchanged. The native resume identity explicitly excludes concurrency. Hashes of all 3,368 prior graded answers are saved. The 32-request baseline averaged 2,356 generated tokens/second over 30 recent serving-log samples; the 64-request comparison has not begun. At 18:05:41 UTC, the hub’s `federation-sync-cw-us-east-02a` thread crashed with `rigging.filesystem.cross_region.TransferBudgetExceeded` after exhausting its 10 GB cross-region transfer budget. A live thread profile confirms the sync thread is absent while the heartbeat remains alive; 231 handoffs were pending to that peer. This is a shared handoff failure, not GPU generation slowness. Operator recovery is needed; the transfer guard and shared controller were left unchanged. The queued job retains the original deadline. The prior job and its children have termination events at 18:33:04 UTC, and the regional backend reports no remaining matching pods; hub status remained stale. No overlapping GPU server was launched.

<details>
<summary>Recovery decisions and earlier failure</summary>

Before recovery: **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it thinking-off is partial: 5,091 graded / 5,200, with 109 model-connection failures (`APIConnectionError`); thinking-on has not run.** The corrected cluster-only submission passed model preparation and generated answers through TaskCompendium and Marin/vLLM. The runner then raised `EvaluationInfrastructureError`; its serving worker and broker are stopped. FineStore preserves successful grades and failed-attempt evidence for recovery. Do not report the available-grade aggregate as a complete benchmark score. Recorded usage for the completed responses: 7,145,508 input and 1,392,082 output tokens. After explicit authorization to fix the failed run, recovery job `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-recovery-20261113` was submitted on November 13. The private launcher now calls the existing `execute_with_retries` wrapper (up to three native passes per mode) instead of single-pass `execute`. Successful attempts are skipped on resume; hashes of the 5,091 graded responses were saved for verification. The model, protocol, seed, cap, and concurrency are unchanged. This recovery is bounded to two H100s for two hours (at most four additional H100-hours); no core-code change or unbounded resubmission was added. The lower-level cause of the connection failures remains unconfirmed.

</details>

Both modes were prepared with a 16,384-token total output cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, seed 42, and the checkpoint’s top-k 64 default. CPU preparation and the pinned tokenizer’s thinking-switch check passed; both published inputs contain byte-identical question/evaluation shards for all 5,200 questions. The intended comparison uses one two-H100 server, off then on. Truncations remain zero-scored. This measures a policy-relevant open-weight model, not paper parity.

<details>
<summary>Paired Gemma run provenance</summary>

Model revision: `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`; adapter/runtime revision: `fe813e34c2`. Reuse the existing cohort model configuration, compilation and CUDA graphs, corpus publication, native evaluation worker, packaged grader, and FineStore. Separate corpus protocols change only `enable_thinking`; the same questions, prompt, generation cap, and aggregation apply to both. Unlike the earlier SimpleQA example’s 2,048/16,384 split, equal caps avoid confounding thinking with output allowance. No new public launcher or core code is added. Raw artifacts remain controlled; publish only audited aggregates.

Iris replacement job: `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-paired-r2-20261113`. The original job was cancelled before GPU inference: the private launcher incorrectly constrained the region to `US-EAST-02A`, producing a node selector that excluded all 36 nodes. The corrected submission uses cluster-only placement, matching the standard launcher. Both original jobs were confirmed stopped. The replacement retains the original 2026-11-13 02:22 UTC deadline rather than resetting its four-hour allowance. A submitted job is not a completed or scored benchmark. Audit selection and grading counts, reasoning/final separation, truncations, parse failures, and all twelve cells before reporting full results. Preserve partial FineStore artifacts if the time bound is reached; do not silently extend the budget.

</details>

Historical model validation (2026-11-06, **Evalchemy path**):

**Llama-4 Maverick completed all 5,200 questions through native Evalchemy and FineStore.** All 12 cell counts and macro aggregation were checked. Combined macro: **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ results. BCQ: **57.43%**; MCQ: **43.77%**. Unweighted accuracy: **47.46% (2,468/5,200)**.

| Biological subtask | Paper combined | Run combined | Difference (percentage points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 45.70% | 46.70% | +1.00 |
| Splice sites | 38.00% | 37.50% | −0.50 |
| Taxonomy | 56.60% | 61.90% | +5.30 |
| Histone marks | 42.10% | 42.90% | +0.80 |
| TFBS | 43.00% | 43.60% | +0.60 |
| Motifs | 69.00% | 71.00% | +2.00 |
| Overall macro | 49.07% | 50.60% | +1.53 |

Combined paper values are derived from [Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05774v1#S4.T2). This is a development comparison, not exact replication: providers, precision, stochastic sampling, parser, and explicit output cap can differ.

There were **six parse failures, no scored refusals, and no output-limit truncations**. Maverick had no separate thinking control enabled, consistent with its paper configuration; the prompt still requests visible analysis. Reported API cost was **$3.08** (conservative accounting bound **$3.93**), excluding CPU hosting and the connectivity pilot.

TaskCompendium migration validation (2026-11-12, `fe813e34c2`): **all 5,200 saved requests and responses were replayed with zero prompt, per-item metric, or extracted-answer differences**. All **120 grouped metric comparisons** match, preserving the full-run results above. This reuses the existing generation run; it is not a new full-benchmark run.

A separate **two-question live native smoke** (one BCQ, one MCQ; Maverick/Parasail FP8) completed through the published corpus, context selection, ChatModel, RolloutEngine, isolated packaged grader, and FineStore. Both attempts were graded without parsing or infrastructure failures. Usage: **1,982 input + 348 output tokens**, zero reported reasoning tokens; API cost **$0.0010417**, excluding CPU hosting. No retries or GPUs were used for inference. The same two-question path also passed a no-cost preflight using saved HTTP responses.

<details>
<summary>Migration validation scope and execution differences</summary>

The replay compared current messages with both historical HTTP requests and FineStore samples, selected final content, and checked every stored metric and extracted answer. Six historical parse failures remain unchanged. Group comparisons cover six metrics across the six subtasks, two formats, and twelve cells.

The live wire sent seed 42 and `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": true}`; the historical OpenRouter calls omitted both. Temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and the 16,384-token cap match. Sending these fields does not prove provider enforcement or hidden-reasoning support. The smoke validates execution, not score parity or statistical performance.

The smoke used the standard BASIC_GRADER lock builder and the pinned tokenizer loaded with `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`. `AutoTokenizer` failed on a field-type mismatch in the pinned model configuration; therefore the automatic launcher/tokenizer-loading path is not validated. Public launcher access, dashboard ingestion, and production reporting remain separate. No implementation changes were needed for replay or smoke validation.

Setup-only attempts encountered an omitted input file and unintended Iris child-worker selection during publication; they made no model requests and were stopped. The successful CPU job used the already-published corpus, made exactly two model requests, and finished with archived outputs verified. Raw evidence remains private.

TaskCompendium validation (2026-11-10): **all 5,200 pinned questions pass conversion and reference-answer grading**, with correct cell populations, equal cell weights, and an unchanged prompt hash. All **23 GenomeQA tests** pass, including native publication and fixed-budget selection. The TaskCompendium suite passed **714 tests (4 skipped)** before the declaration-only sampling fix. Lint passes and all advisory findings are addressed. Another **103 integration tests** passed, and TaskCompendium’s typecheck reports **zero errors**. The Iris container could not run a bubblewrap-dependent task-driver check. **CI is green at `bbcd396f89`**, including TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, Marin unit/integration, lint, and docs; this is separate from the container’s limitation. No model had been rerun through TaskCompendium at that point.

</details>

Remaining work:

- Validate Marin ingestion and dashboard reporting, preserving macro scores, six primary subtask views, all secondary results, and coverage. Do not infer correct counts or pooled-binomial intervals from the macro.
- Implement public sample-access restrictions before adding Marin launcher registration or exposing these runs in public dashboard records. Native run artifacts remain controlled.
- Migration #10957 merged as `2af3f828aa` on November 13 (UTC). #10984 now targets `main`; update `63659f290a` integrates main `a922ffc740`, preserves its task-source deduplication, and retains `EvaluationCorpusRecipe` / `prepare_evaluation`. Controlled curation remains available; public launcher/catalog registration remains disabled. Changed-file lint and all 23 GenomeQA tests pass against this base. Broader remote validation is not green: Harbor had 1,889 passes and 26 failures, with the identical failure list reproduced on unchanged main; the selected workspace suite had 162 passes, 14 failures, and five errors versus 161 passes and the same failures/errors on main (the extra pass is GenomeQA publication). These comparisons establish no new failures in this environment, not a clean full-suite result. **GitHub CI is green at `63659f290a`**, including TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, Marin unit/integration, Harbor, lint, and docs. This supersedes the remote-container limitations for landing validation. The active Gemma recovery retains its frozen `fe813e34c2` runtime bundle; these code checks do not constitute a new model run.
- Before evaluating other models/backends, pin reasoning effort, sampling exceptions, provider-specific enforcement of the shared cap, and preservation of finish/refusal metadata. Official-policy admission is a separate decision; further runs need explicit scope and bounds.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered and rationale</summary>

| Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale and tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use pinned HF `binary` and `mcq` data. | Load the authors’ twelve JSONL files directly; rebuild questions from upstream biological databases. | All 5,200 HF rows matched the author release on evaluation fields. HF fits existing loading components. Direct JSONL would also be valid but offers little functional benefit after the equivalence check. Rebuilding could change sampling, filtering, and questions. Metadata equivalence remains unchecked. |
| Evaluate the original full benchmark. | Carbon’s modified MCQ dataset; 600-row or organism-specific subsets. | Preserve the original six task families and both formats. Carbon changes the taxonomy task; subsets change coverage. Neither should silently replace the original benchmark. |
| Use TaskCompendium’s existing evaluation components. | Retain the first vendored Evalchemy adapter; adopt the authors’ runner or Carbon’s Inspect evaluator. | The new-evaluation architecture supersedes the original Evalchemy decision. Reuse acquisition, conversion, grader packaging, and protocol/group metadata; preserve the benchmark independently of its original runner. The migration has since merged; reuse its native corpus path without adding public launcher registration. |
| Reuse the grader’s existing stop-reason channel. | Add a new transport for complete provider metadata. | Keep truncation handling without expanding the runtime. Explicit refusals without a `content_filter` stop reason score zero but are classified as missing answers; original provider messages remain in the raw archive. |
| Retain existing runtime failure, retry, and coverage behavior. | Add opt-in empty-response and strict-completeness policies. | These concerns apply across benchmarks and do not justify shared runtime changes for GenomeQA. Remove the proposed policies and their tests; inspect coverage before reporting complete results. |
| Report raw accuracy. | Normalize accuracy relative to chance. | Ordinary correct/total accuracy is interpretable and preserves the paper’s metric. BCQ and MCQ have different chance levels; retain their separate results rather than changing the metric to compensate. |
| Weight the six subtasks equally and the two formats equally. | Pool all 5,200 questions into micro-accuracy. | Pooling would give motifs five times less weight than each other family because it has fewer questions. Equal weighting treats each biological capability as one component. |
| Foreground six subtask scores and their overall mean. | Foreground BCQ/MCQ summaries; show only a combined score; show only the two format scores. | The research priority is understanding biological strengths and weaknesses. First average BCQ/MCQ within each subtask, then average subtasks. Reversing that order gives the same overall number with equal weights; the decision concerns presentation. Keep all 12 cells and both format summaries as secondary diagnostics. |
| Retain the authors’ fixed optimized system prompt and user layout. | Minimal generic prompting; Carbon’s Inspect multiple-choice prompt; repeat prompt optimization. | Use an established prompt for the original questions and avoid introducing an additional variable. Optimization already occurred offline; the fixed prompt is in the public runner. The resulting scores measure capability with supplied biological guidance. Generic prompting could support a separate ablation, but is not part of this integration. |
| Reuse shared final-response cleanup, then a small GenomeQA-specific letter parser. | Copy the authors’ complete parser; use the shared HLE/GPQA extractors unchanged; introduce a separate extraction implementation. | Synthetic checks showed that existing first/last-letter extractors can select incidental analysis or trailing letters. The custom parser handles final-section isolation, explicit declarations, conflicts, and valid options; shared response representation and thinking cleanup are reused. This deliberately adapts the author parser rather than claiming exact extraction parity. |
| Accept an unambiguous explicit `Answer: X` when the heading is missing. | Require the exact `### Answer` heading for every response. | A clearly stated answer should not be marked wrong solely for omitting a heading. Conflicting markers and missing answers still require focused validation; do not recover answers from hidden reasoning. |
| Apply one shared total generated-token cap across models. | Model-specific recommended caps; leave limits to provider defaults as the author runner does; cap only the answer text. | Bound generation consistently across a large question set. Include reasoning, visible analysis, and final answer. This equalizes nominal token allowance, not compute, latency, or tokenizer efficiency. Provider semantics must be verified. |
| Start with 16,384 generated tokens per question. | Start with 32,768 tokens. | Limit cost and latency over 5,200 questions. The tighter cap may increase truncations; report them by model and subtask. This is an initial evaluation choice, not a budget validated by the GenomeQA paper. |
| Enable thinking where supported and pin effort per model configuration. | Always use provider-recommended mode, including thinking off; use the same named effort for every model; use maximum effort everywhere. | Follow the GPQA/MMLU-Pro thinking-on pattern in the current policy. Identical effort labels do not imply equivalent reasoning across providers, and maximum effort may exhaust the total budget before an answer. Concrete effort values remain to be specified per model. |
| Request temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95. | Provider-recommended sampling; temperature 0 as in MMLU-Pro; Carbon-X’s 0.6/0.95/top-k 20 settings. | Retain the settings requested by the released GenomeQA runner alongside its prompt. Marin’s reasoning-Q&A precedents are mixed: GPQA uses 0.7, MMLU-Pro uses greedy generation. This is a GenomeQA protocol choice, not a universal Marin rule. Document unsupported provider parameters and deviations. |
| First-pass paper comparison: Llama-4 Maverick on the complete TF-motif MCQ cell (100 questions). | No paper-model check; a full 5,200-question run; a 600-question stratified sample across all 12 cells; the complete enhancer/promoter MCQ cell (500 questions). | A complete cell permits direct comparison with an entry in the paper’s table; a cross-cell sample would use different question coverage. Motif MCQ is the smallest complete cell, and Maverick avoids reasoning-effort ambiguity. This was the initial scope. The later authorized full-benchmark validation is recorded above; retain the small check as historical evidence and retire its temporary integration code. |
| Proceed with independently written integration code and runtime HF loading; do not redistribute benchmark questions. | Wait indefinitely for author permission; vendor the upstream code, prompt, and dataset together. | An author response is not a prerequisite for adapter development. Keep the dataset license explicitly unspecified, use synthetic test fixtures, and keep question text out of public artifacts. Runtime fetching reduces redistribution but does not resolve missing dataset-use terms. |
| Keep the pinned runner prompt external and load its string without executing upstream code. | Bundle the runner prompt; use the CC BY paper’s Figure 8 prompt; write a new prompt. | Figure 8 is shorter than the runner: it omits the explicit binary-letter instruction and some reasoning guidance. Using it would change the agreed protocol. External loading preserves that protocol without bundling the prompt; it does not establish a license for the external asset. |

Batch submission was also considered: no Maverick batch endpoint was listed during validation. The run used concurrent synchronous requests, following the existing evaluation pattern, rather than adding batch infrastructure. Carbon’s Inspect evaluator uses a modified MCQ dataset and different prompting; its scores are not a parity target for this integration.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Detailed validation, parser analysis, and operational record</summary>

| Subtask | BCQ paper | BCQ run | MCQ paper | MCQ run | Combined paper | Combined run |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 55.40 | 56.60 | 36.00 | 36.80 | 45.70 | 46.70 |
| Splice sites | 50.00 | 49.80 | 26.00 | 25.20 | 38.00 | 37.50 |
| Taxonomy | 57.00 | 61.40 | 56.20 | 62.40 | 56.60 | 61.90 |
| Histone marks | 52.60 | 52.60 | 31.60 | 33.20 | 42.10 | 42.90 |
| TFBS | 51.60 | 49.20 | 34.40 | 38.00 | 43.00 | 43.60 |
| Motifs | 73.00 | 75.00 | 65.00 | 67.00 | 69.00 | 71.00 |
| Macro | 56.60 | 57.43 | 41.53 | 43.77 | 49.07 | 50.60 |

The full run used `meta-llama/llama-4-maverick` through the native CLI, LMBackend, grader, reducer, and FineStore at `e426d0027a810f621c28a24d1d34abf523caa254`. Archived evidence contains 5,200 unique prompts and provider response IDs. Each of the first five subtasks has 500 questions per format; motifs have 100 per format.

Provider transition: preserve 150 DigitalOcean completions and generate the remaining 5,050 with Parasail FP8 after shared-provider rate limits. Preserve wrong answers as well as correct ones. Concurrency was one, then two; the cumulative $75 API ceiling was retained. No model reruns were selected based on wrong answers.

Verified requests used temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and max output 16,384. No separate reasoning control or reasoning response content was present. Prompt lengths were 822–2,494 tokens and fit the context window. Usage: **6,716,430 input tokens, 1,493,571 output tokens, zero reported reasoning tokens**. Visible analysis is ordinary output, not evidence of a separate reasoning mode.

Six final choices used “The answer is X” or “The correct answer is X” instead of `Answer: X`. The fallback encountered incidental letters in the final section, including K in K562, and rejected conflicting candidates. Four failures were splice-site MCQ, one histone MCQ, and one TFBS MCQ. Only splice-site MCQ ID 258 would become correct (D). Recovering all six would yield macro 50.6167%, MCQ 43.80%, and 2,469 correct. These are diagnostic counterfactuals; reported scores remain unchanged, and natural-language declaration recovery was not added. The later explicit multi-option rejection fix is recorded below.

Reported API cost: $3.077122105, excluding the $0.0000145 connectivity pilot and CPU cost. There were 46 HTTP 429 responses and two whitespace-only HTTP 200 responses; existing transport handling retried them. The latter have no usage record. Reserving possible charges and using undiscounted input pricing yields the $3.932851485 accounting bound. The replacement portion took 2h 41m 47s, excluding the earlier DigitalOcean portion. Raw artifacts and checksums remain in controlled storage.

The earlier complete 100-question motif-MCQ check scored 64/100 versus the paper’s 65/100; [historical evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10981#issuecomment-6689477380) is retained. A complete cell was chosen over a cross-cell sample to permit a direct table comparison; the later full run addressed its limited coverage.

Historical review/cleanup: `1a676d52de` retired the 100-question check (lint and 45 tests passed). Independent review corrected descriptions of custom parsing and metadata-dependent truncation/refusal detection in `83256403f9`. Loom fixes in `d60a229dd1` rejected explicit multiple answers and corrected false-positive override tests; 50 focused tests passed, and an offline comparison found no changed candidate sets across the 5,200 saved responses. Loom separately reported 27 GenomeQA tests passing.

`ef61262b78` removed the launcher/configuration/egress entries because public dashboard sample browsing could expose upstream assets; CI passed on that adapter-only revision. The earlier Iris queue-deadline test failure reproduced using unchanged main test/monitor code (`e0bc917ee549f15dd30e3c97ce3ff8d690b43440`): its fixture marked a job RUNNING without running-task metadata. No Iris fix or subsequent model rerun is claimed. The TaskCompendium port supersedes these historical vendored files and override checks.

TaskCompendium port (2026-11-10): commits `c3885c3a06`, `5f586ea963`, `9c0f85c8aa`, and `bbcd396f89` replace the vendored adapter with a source declaration, converter, packaged scorer, and protocol on main `7f0ed8cb52`. The source-grader package lives under the existing `importers.evalchemy` directory for reuse; it does not import or execute vendored Evalchemy. The shared changes are final-only response selection, scorer registration, and an explicit stop-reason argument populated by the existing grader environment at the script entry point. The existing output-budget policy enforces 16,384 tokens without a GenomeQA runtime override gate.

Validation: 23 GenomeQA tests pass at `bbcd396f89`; 714 TaskCompendium tests passed with four skips before its declaration-only fix, and 103 other integration tests pass at the final head. Pyrefly reports zero errors. The task-driver check was container-blocked (bubblewrap namespace creation is not permitted), not a claimed local pass. Subsequent selected CI checks passed at `bbcd396f89` on 2026-11-10. No sandbox permissions were changed.

The six advisory lanes completed; findings about environment access, the unused callback argument, and repeated budget/weight values were fixed. Offline full-source checks and synthetic tests use no model calls. The broader integration checks run on CPU with one pytest worker, the existing async-test plugin, and Iris auto-detection disabled inside pytest; early setup attempts omitted support files or inherited unsuitable worker/backend/plugin defaults and do not count as validation. The integration test caught missing explicit `top_k`/`stop` fields; `bbcd396f89` supplies unset/empty values matching the protocol.

Migration #10957 was verified open at `9f4a58169e6366ecfb66c39ab24895abf43732e9`. Removing this PR’s old-schema launcher YAML avoids that particular migration conflict, but deletion of the vendored source still required a port/landing-order decision at that point. The subsequently authorized TaskCompendium port is described above. The declaration compatibility fix was implemented within #10984 before #10957 merged; no changes to the migration PR were made.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Pinned assets, scoring protocol, and implementation boundaries</summary>

Data: [`HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943), revision `e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943`; only `binary/train-00000-of-00001.parquet` and `mcq/train-00000-of-00001.parquet`. The split name `train` does not change their role as evaluation questions. Preserve DNA text and option order; identify questions by `(format, subtask, id)` and never expose answer/metadata fields to the model. The 2026-11-05 comparison found zero mismatches in question, ordered options, answer index, or answer text, with no missing/extra rows; metadata equivalence was not checked.

- Binary SHA-256: `0ef4c3d33541980e3fded9a5b23a952296ce3c51cb0415b42c0299a61c21938a`.
- MCQ SHA-256: `c1cbb51449eb8a5241890337c88dc1bc0a58974b8eb4cb8bc49f310b12faeb75`.
- Prompt/protocol reference: authors’ [run.py](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py), commit `7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d`. Extract the literal prompt string as data; do not execute it. Preserve the original user-message layout. Prompt-development-set disjointness has not been established.

For cell accuracy `a[s,f] = correct / questions`:

```text
subtask[s] = (a[s,BCQ] + a[s,MCQ]) / 2
overall = mean(subtask[s] over six subtasks)
BCQ = mean(a[s,BCQ] over six subtasks)
MCQ = mean(a[s,MCQ] over six subtasks)
```

Format macros match the authors’ [aggregation](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/collect_res.py). Reversing the two averaging steps gives the same overall value. Declare weighted-mean reduction: weight 5 for motif questions and 1 otherwise on `genomeqa_macro`; keep ordinary accuracy unweighted. Item groups retain all breakdowns for downstream reduction. Chance levels are 50% BCQ, 25% MCQ, and 37.5% combined; do not chance-correct or promote internal question labels to additional equal-weight tasks.

Parser: reuse shared final-response representation and thinking-marker cleanup before applying a GenomeQA-specific letter parser. Isolate the last `### Answer` section and check valid options. Without that heading, accept an unambiguous explicit `Answer: X`. Reject conflicting declarations; do not search hidden reasoning or apply an unrestricted last-letter fallback to the whole response. A completion reported as length-truncated scores zero even if it contains a candidate answer. Missing or unparseable final answers and reported provider refusals score zero when graded. TaskCompendium passes stop reasons through its existing grader environment: `length` is truncation and `content_filter` is refusal. Final-only selection suppresses explicit refusal content, but a refusal field without `content_filter` is diagnosed as a missing answer, not a separately counted refusal. The raw attempt retains the original provider message. This avoids adding a new completion-metadata transport for one benchmark; validate metadata preservation per backend.

Reuse existing empty-response, checkpoint, retry, and task-validity behavior. Empty responses may be retried or mostly-empty runs rejected. Transport failures remain ungraded. Check expected/generated/graded counts before calling results complete; available-grade aggregates are partial results, not complete-benchmark scores. No new runtime completeness gate is part of this adapter.

Generation: the author runner requests 0.7/0.95 and thinking where supported but no explicit output cap; historical provider budgets are not fully pinned. Our 16,384 cap includes all generated tokens. Prefer a native combined cap; if a provider only supports independent hard caps, their allocations must sum to 16,384 and remain to be chosen for that route. Flag unenforceable equivalents. Do not truncate DNA inputs or selectively increase budgets. Verify effective requests after model overrides, recording exceptions, effort, usage, and finish reasons.

The TaskCompendium port uses pinned `HfSource`/`UrlSource` acquisition and `EvalDataset`, a GenomeQA converter, existing `source_package` script packaging, and an `EvaluationProtocol` with `WEIGHTED_MEAN`. It emits `metric_weights` and subtask/format/cell groups; main does not yet produce headline summaries from this path. The only response-policy extension is `final_only`; the scorer reuses verifyit’s thinking-marker cleanup. No runtime retry policy or reducer is added.

Configure the run with at least the protocol’s 16,384-token allowance and the served tokenizer. The existing required-output budget excludes rows if the configured cap is below 16,384 or the full prompt plus that allowance cannot fit; it does not silently lower the allowance. Inspect the effective settings and require all 5,200 rows before reporting a full-protocol result. This uses common runtime behavior instead of retaining the old adapter’s custom override/preflight gates.

Downstream validation must exercise the native FineStore reader, record construction, and dashboard measurement path with unequal cell sizes, missing coverage, and macro differing from micro. Preserve metric identities and actual counts. Additional scalar metrics alone do not create six dashboard columns; views must use the same generated outputs without double-counting or rerunning questions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Asset-use rationale and Carbon comparison</summary>

At inspection, the authors’ repository had no declared license and the HF card had no dataset license. The paper describes code/data availability and open academic/research source databases; that does not establish reuse terms for the assembled release. Proceed with independently written integration and runtime fetching, without claiming the rights are settled or inheriting Apache-2.0/CC BY. Keep synthetic tests in the repository and raw questions/response echoes in controlled storage. Public reports contain aggregates and diagnostics. Redistribution remains a separate decision if terms become available.

The paper is CC BY 4.0, but Figure 8 differs from the runner prompt: it omits the explicit binary-letter instruction and some reasoning guidance. Substitution would alter the protocol. Keep the pinned runner prompt external rather than bundling it or silently replacing it with Figure 8.

The [Carbon-X card](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceBio/Carbon-X) reports 0.6/0.95/top-k 20, thinking disabled, one sample. Its [evaluator](https://github.com/huggingface/carbon/blob/4ca3ce3e5c55e5821d6068bac5c6e3806027a26f/carbon-x/evaluation/evaluate.py) reads local sampling from `generation_config.json`; endpoint sampling defaults are unset unless overridden. Local GenomeQA output allowance is context length minus 17,408 tokens. These are public defaults, not verified historical API payloads.

Carbon’s [GenomeQA task](https://github.com/huggingface/carbon/blob/4ca3ce3e5c55e5821d6068bac5c6e3806027a26f/carbon-x/evaluation/tasks/genomeqa.py) uses Inspect `multiple_choice(cot=True)` and `choice()` on modified MCQ data from `DNAIntelligenceIndex`, replacing broad taxonomy with within-eukaryote classification and omitting the original optimized system prompt. A Carbon-protocol comparison would be a separate evaluation. Marin [policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) supplies mixed sampling precedents (GPQA 0.7, MMLU-Pro greedy) and thinking-on overrides, not a universal provider-default rule.

</details>

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Propose **BiomniBench-DA public-50 with five derived-input variants** as a candidate in-distribution (ID) development evaluation for Marin. Review the protocol and collect external-model evidence before deciding whether to add it to the ID policy. No Marin models, including Snowball, will be evaluated until that policy decision.

Use Marin's standard evaluation launcher and the selected BixBench harness/judge settings, while retaining Biomni's tasks, grading rubrics and 60-minute agent budget. Our Daytona eval account rejects the authors' 16 GiB RAM / 20 GiB disk requests, so the proposal caps resources at 8/10 GiB and documents the affected inputs. This is a modified public-subset protocol; it does not reproduce the paper's full-benchmark scores.

The Qwen control task (`da-4-6`) completed with a signed score of 28/100 and unsigned comparison of 38/100. Both required reports and the graded verifier result were read back from the archive. EvalDash's API reports continuous reward 0.28 with 1/1 scored coverage; visual rendering and independent audit of the judge's decisions remain pending. The remaining three pilot cases are in image preparation; full baselines remain pending.

## Description

[BiomniBench-DA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235) contains biomedical data-analysis tasks requiring executable analysis and written reports. Use all 50 public tasks at revision `e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235`, retaining the five modified-input tasks in the denominator. The [paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.12.724604v2.full) reports aggregates over 100 tasks and three repetitions. We have not found author scores for the public 50 or saved per-task judgments that establish scoring parity.

The evaluation would measure multi-step analysis and reporting for ID development. Its incremental value beyond BixBench still needs evidence: task-content comparison alone does not establish different model rankings or useful checkpoint-selection signals. This proposal follows the external-baseline and evidence pattern in [SimpleQA Verified #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).

The existing [task-content comparison with BixBench public 205](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6781595235) reviews all 50 BiomniBench prompts/input descriptions, all 205 BixBench questions and 12 selected BiomniBench rubrics. It identifies candidate additional coverage in censored survival analysis, TCR repertoire interpretation, cell–cell communication, gene co-expression networks and chromatin analysis. Its manual inventory labels 27 tasks as substantially overlapping, 11 as extensions and 12 as distinctive workflows; these are granularity-dependent judgments, not a measured redundancy rate. The comparison motivates this proposal but does not establish different model rankings, reliable grading or feasibility of the five modified-input tasks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether the public tasks remain valid under the disclosed resource and input changes, whether scoring is reproducible and auditable, and whether the benchmark adds useful coverage beyond BixBench.

Review requested:

- Are the resource/input changes and signed-penalty scoring acceptable for an ID proposal, subject to validation below?
- What additional evidence is needed to establish value beyond BixBench?
- Confirm implementation placement before policy adoption. The pilot uses the existing Harbor path; TaskCompendium/TaskSpec migration is deferred during protocol investigation. That does not establish an exception to the guidance that new evaluation implementations belong in TaskCompendium.

## Proposed protocol

| Component | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Population | All 50 public tasks; no exclusions based on model performance. Report the aggregate and separate 45 unchanged-input / five derived-input summaries. |
| Sandbox | Daytona; preserve each task's native CPU/GPU allocation (2 CPUs, no GPU); RAM = min(native, 8 GiB), disk = min(native, 10 GiB). The release requests 16/20 GiB for 48 tasks and 4/10 GiB for two. |
| Time limits | 3,600 seconds for the agent; 900 seconds for the verifier. Setup and serving startup are separate. |
| Harness | Pi through Marin's standard launcher and vendored Harbor. Pilot pin: Pi 0.87.0. The selected BixBench YAML does not pin Pi; the final baseline version still needs agreement. |
| Context/output | BixBench policy's 65,536 context / 16,384 per-response output settings, with its compaction behavior and model-specific reasoning settings. Verify effective requests. |
| Judge | MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, using the selected BixBench campaign's dedicated-server configuration. Preserve Biomni's rubric and grading prompt. |
| Judge request | Pilot candidate: temperature 0, 8,192 output tokens, 120-second request timeout, no SDK retries; outer verifier limit 900 seconds. These are explicit Biomni pilot settings, not a claim of identical BixBench request settings. |
| Baselines | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B first, then Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and GPT-OSS-20B. Use pinned campaign configurations and record effective reasoning settings. No Marin/Snowball models. |
| Attempts | Pilot: one attempt, no automatic trial retries. Proposed full baseline: three independent solver repetitions per task, subject to protocol and compute-budget agreement. Agree on uncertainty estimation and invalid-output/timeout/recovery rules before launch. Operational retries and judge-only recovery are not independent repetitions; do not take a best-of score. |
| Concurrency | One trial for the initial control; two proposed for the four-case pilot. Concurrency is an operational setting. |
| Evidence | Preserve per-task submissions, trajectories, judge responses, rubric decisions, failures and provenance; validate continuous-score reporting through EvalDash. |

The pilot uses Marin commit `246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7`, with local adapter/preparation files and a bundle-inclusion change. It is not an unchanged main-only execution. Freeze the complete source, image and input manifests for baseline runs. The copied Qwen configuration pins model revision `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`; remaining baseline revisions must be recorded before their runs.

## Changes from the release

Live create requests against the Daytona eval account rejected 16 GiB RAM and 20 GiB disk with explicit per-sandbox maxima of 8 GiB and 10 GiB. These are verified account constraints, not universal Daytona limits. The current choice is the closest supported allocation on this account without requesting a limit increase.

| IDs | Change | Reason and validation required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01–M02 | For `da-1-3` and `da-1-4`, omit the approximately 19.18 GB expression matrix `GSE236581_counts.mtx`; retain clinical and cell metadata. | The matrix exceeds the disk limit. Verify that retained data supports every rubric requirement; expression-based annotations can no longer be rederived. |
| M03–M05 | For `da-17-1`, `da-17-3` and `da-17-5`, replace the approximately 12.22 GB lupus H5AD with the pinned 2.64 GB raw-count derivative. | Preserve all cells and required metadata within the disk limit. Validate gene/cell/donor alignment and task-specific feasibility; normalized expression and embeddings are absent. |
| M06–M07 | Disclose the five input changes in task instructions and remove copies of deliberately omitted files from image recipes. | Prevent assumptions about unavailable data; retain exact prompt/recipe diffs and file hashes. |
| M08 | Existing adapter normalizes `da-20-3`'s 72 JSON-form Docker `COPY` entries to a directory copy. | Historical workaround for Daytona Dockerfile parsing. Apply only if needed by the prepared-image path; verify identical paths and bytes with no extra files. |
| M09 | Cap RAM/disk at 8/10 GiB; preserve smaller native requests and native CPU/GPU. | The confirmed account ceilings reduce the computational budget. Record requested/enforced resources and OOM/disk failures; input fit alone does not prove analysis feasibility. |
| M10 | Replace the release's judge provider implementation with the selected MiniMax judge through Marin's verifier connection. | Align judge model/serving with the selected BixBench campaign. This can change grading decisions and requires auditing. |
| M11 | Apply signed rubric penalties; retain an unsigned comparison score from the same decisions. | The written rubric includes negative points that the released parser drops. This is an intentional scoring change. |
| M12 | Require complete, unique criterion judgments with valid levels/reasons; reject malformed or truncated judge responses. | Treat grader failures as unscored, rather than silently accepting incomplete grades. Error and recovery rates can differ from the release. |
| M13 | Prepare digest-pinned images with Pi/verifier dependencies; adapt verifier connection variables and export continuous `reward`. | Required by the current Marin path. The control image needed a separate data layer to restore its original input at its original path; runtime checksum validation passed. Preserve build recipes, package versions and hashes. |

If any modified task cannot support a required rubric criterion, that blocks the full-50 protocol. Restore sufficient inputs/resources or seek review of a revised protocol before running full baselines; do not count input-induced impossibility as model failure or silently exclude the task.

<details>
<summary>Lupus derivative construction and provenance</summary>

The lupus derivative retains `obs`, `raw` and `uns`, rebuilds `var` from `raw.var`, and links root `X` to `raw.X`. It retains all cells; it is not cell subsampling. Both `X` and `raw.X` contain raw counts. Other root groups, including the original normalized matrix and embeddings, are omitted. The original container filename is retained.

- [Pinned derivative](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83): revision `60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83`, file `lupus-raw-counts.h5ad`, 2,642,705,030 bytes.
- Derived SHA-256: `33179d1cf993091dc0bd41372629534f6b7da1ce1114d74c36110ffbee375d53`.
- Original SHA-256: `7ba85edbdc033a9aeeecabe7a1cfcb0660282cc24b04f49fb52dd3825052c620`.
- These values come from the existing adapter. Rehash downloaded bytes before use; preserve the conversion recipe, source attribution and license. Record the CRC matrix's source hash and all prepared-file hashes in the final manifest.

</details>

## Scoring and failure handling

Preserve `/app/trace.md`, `/app/answer.txt` and the source rubrics. The judge reads agent-authored reports; it does not independently verify every reported action. Audit sampled judgments against the captured tool trajectory.

For each task, sum signed rubric points, retain the raw total, and clamp to `[0, 100]`. Average the clamped per-task scores. Thus a raw −5 is reported as zero, and a reliability penalty of −10 reduces otherwise perfect work from 100 to 90. The released parser's unsigned calculation would yield 100 in the latter case. Neither calculation is established as the one used for the paper's results.

Export `reward = score / 100` for Marin's continuous metric path, preserving the 0–100 score, raw signed total and unsigned comparison in the evidence. Verify EvalDash's displayed scale; report mean rubric score, not accuracy.

The selected runner does not yet guarantee this failure contract: with no exception and a present `verifier_result`, `_read_trial` marks the trial scored even when `rewards.reward` is missing, defaulting its value to zero ([source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L207-L233)). This is confirmed by code inspection, not an end-to-end control. Add missing, nonnumeric and nonfinite reward controls alongside a valid zero; verify scored coverage as well as the aggregate. Resolve any demonstrated adapter/shared-runner defect in a scoped PR before full baselines.

Proposed failure handling:

- Confirmed empty submissions receive zero; grade partial submissions and flag them. Confirm emptiness only after successful inspection of the stopped agent's output location and successful collection. Missing files in an incomplete archive do not establish emptiness. Distinguish confirmed empty output from collection failure in result metadata before full baselines.
- Setup, collection and judge failures remain unscored. Failure to collect a report is not evidence that the report was empty.
- On agent timeout, establish that the agent stopped before capturing and grading its submission. This behavior still needs live validation for the selected runtime.
- Judge-only recovery reuses the same saved submission, rubric and judge settings; retain both original and recovery records. Record any solver rerun separately.
- Report graded coverage and all failures. An incomplete scored-task mean is not a complete 50-task score. Resolve retry/invalid-output rules before full baselines: the paper specifies a retry for invalid/missing output and then zero, which differs from the current pilot's zero retries and proposed unscored infrastructure failures.

Preserve the source instructions' paper-lookup restrictions. Record network access and installed packages; the current environment permits runtime installation and does not fully pin transitive dependencies. The unchanged-input group still shares resource, harness, judge and scorer changes; its score is not native-protocol parity.

## Status

Evidence collected on 2026-11-13:

| Check | Result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Resource limits | Live requests confirmed the eval account's 8 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk ceilings. |
| Scorer replay | Local controls reproduce signed 100/95/90 versus unsigned 100/100/100 for reliability levels A/B/C. These are synthetic judgments, not model scores. |
| Empty submission | An intentionally empty local submission directory emits zero and makes no judge call. The current `missing_submission` label does not itself distinguish confirmed emptiness from failed collection; this control does not validate remote collection-failure handling. |
| Control environment (`da-4-6`) | Remote validation passed for Pi, Python/R, verifier dependencies, the original input checksum and sandbox closure. This does not validate the other 49 tasks or live judging. |
| Standard launcher | Qwen control completed: 28/100 signed, 38/100 unsigned, both reports preserved, verifier status `graded`, 1/1 scored and no recorded trial errors. EvalDash API readback agrees (reward 0.28, continuous metric); this is one control task, not a benchmark-wide score. |
| Remaining execution | Four-case validation (`da-4-6`, `da-1-3`, `da-17-3`, `da-20-3`) and full-50 baselines remain pending. All five derived-input tasks require checks before a full baseline. |

<details>
<summary>Preparation failures and repairs</summary>

Early image preparation failed on an interactive package-install prompt and then on a missing input file; both were repaired before the control evaluation was submitted. A local transport check timed out; the remote worker check subsequently passed. Preserve these negative records in the evidence package. They are not solver failures or zero scores. Historical Luna/GLM diagnostic scores use different settings and will not be pooled into the proposed baselines.

</details>

Before requesting ID adoption:

- [ ] Freeze the final protocol and a 50-row task manifest recording original/derived input hashes, image digests, rubric feasibility, requested/enforced resources and model/Pi/judge revisions. Agree on the proposed three independent solver repetitions and compute budget separately from infrastructure retries and judge recovery. Proposed reporting: mean each task across repetitions, then average tasks equally; report per-repetition means and a task-cluster bootstrap interval, preserving repetitions within each resampled task. Label this as task-sampling uncertainty, not a complete estimate of solver or judge variability.
- [ ] Verify transformed inputs and rubric feasibility for all five affected tasks; validate packaging, enforced resources and task-specific disk/memory use.
- [ ] Exercise good, wrong, partial, confirmed-empty, malformed-judge, missing/invalid-reward and collection-failure controls, plus timeout capture and judge-only recovery; verify coverage and continuous-score display, and audit live judgments against tool traces.
- [ ] Complete external-model public-50 baselines with per-task scores, coverage, 45/five subgroup summaries, failure rates and the agreed uncertainty analysis.
- [ ] Attach the exact pilot patch, preparation recipes and compact validation records; the linked base commit alone does not reproduce the locally modified pilot.
- [ ] Verify archived results and EvalDash ingestion/display; attach reviewable evidence links. Local records are prepared, but a published evidence package is pending.
- [ ] Report wall time, startup/queue time, tokens, sandbox/GPU use, retries, cleanup and measured cost where available. Separate estimates from measurements.
- [ ] Assess incremental coverage beyond BixBench using matched external-model results and documented protocol differences. Reuse suitable existing BixBench evidence where available; additional runs require a separate agreed plan. Three model rankings alone are limited evidence and do not establish checkpoint-selection value. Resolve implementation placement and ownership with evaluation maintainers before the policy decision.

## Links

- [Biology evaluation tracking #9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- [Existing adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) and [adapter source at inspected revision](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/95a4b88b54cae602ade6e79d9536a2c766657301/adapters/biomnibench-da/src/biomnibench_da).
- [Selected BixBench policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/bixbench-pi.yaml) and [MiniMax judge configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/judge-model-configs/MiniMaxAI-MiniMax-M3-MXFP8.yaml).
- [External-baseline evidence precedent #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).
- [Graded Qwen control in EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9). Scorer investigation and complete pilot provenance package: pending attachment before an adoption request.

## Decision Log

Agreed for this investigation: public-50 scope, disclosed resource/input changes, signed scoring with an unsigned comparison, and external baselines starting with Qwen. No Marin-model evaluation before the ID policy decision.

Still open before full baselines: final runtime pins, independent repetitions, uncertainty estimation and failure/recovery rules. Implementation placement, ownership and adoption remain maintainer decisions.

## Conclusion

One control task has completed end-to-end grading and EvalDash API ingestion. There is not yet evidence sufficient to recommend ID adoption. The next decision is whether the proposed deviations and validation plan are acceptable for that assessment.
