issues.title: [evals] Validate BiomniBench-DA public-50 for ID evaluation

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Evaluate Marin Hero on variant effect prediction using unconditioned DNA likelihood, healthy-individual conditioning, and zero-/two-shot classification. The same 100-variant autosomal missense pilot has completed the corrected v3 classification rerun. All 402 reference windows match independent GRCh38 queries; 16 focused offline tests pass. The reserved 300-variant validation remains unrun.

Corrected v3 AUPRC: **0.213 null DNA prefix, 0.302 healthy prefix, 0.110 zero-shot, 0.101 two-shot**. Classification remains weak after fixing the token boundary and using one seeded mapping per variant. V2's standalone-space fix caused extreme EOS preference and is superseded. V3 ends at `Answer:` and scores canonical ` A`/` B` tokens together. All 200 two-shot contexts use matching single-token demonstration answers. [Completed v3 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-report.md). Code and evidence remain on the research branch; no PR or merge is planned.

## Scope: experiment only

This issue tracks a research experiment, not a production feature or a contribution to `main`. Keep experimental code, prompts, analysis, and evidence on the research and harness branches. Opening or reopening PRs, merging code or the archive index into `main`, and production integration are out of scope. Any later promotion requires a separate decision and explicit authorization.

Completion means recording the experiment's results, limitations, and conclusions with reproducible branch-based evidence. It does not require a PR, code review approval, or a merge. Marin PR #11375 and marin-community/marin-logbooks#41 were closed without merging; their branches and commits remain available.

## Description

This experiment measures variant effect prediction (VEP) capability in the Marin Hero SFT model.
MarinDNA supplies the dataset and reference evaluation protocol; VEP-bench supplies the classification input representation.
The pilot supports prompt and scoring iteration before a frozen-method comparison on a fresh, larger development subset.

### Dataset and reference scoring protocol

Reuse the dataset and scoring conventions from the Mendelian evaluation in [Open-Athena/marin-dna](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/tree/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2) as the reference.

- Dataset: `marin-dna/evals_mendelian_traits`, revision `4aed58e50c5dea0b878a665007af2ef9e5108e9f`.
- Split: `train`, which is the project's development split.
- Positives: pathogenic SNVs from OMIM, HGMD, and Smedley et al. 2016, with allele frequency below 0.1%.
- Controls: gnomAD variants with allele frequency above 0.1%.
- Matching: one positive and nine controls per `match_group`, matched within consequence/chromosome strata using distance features.
- Standard likelihood score: compute `LLR = log P(alt) - log P(ref)` for each strand, average forward and reverse-complement LLRs, then negate the average so larger scores indicate predicted pathogenicity.
- Established reporting: per-consequence, global, and macro-average AUPRC, with match-group bootstrap uncertainty.

The DNA-model kernel uses a four-nucleotide softmax and single-base tokens.
Hero's general-vocabulary token likelihoods define a related but different scoring protocol; do not claim numerical parity with that kernel.

### Pilot sample

Use ten complete missense match groups: 100 variants comprising ten pathogenic positives and 90 matched controls.
The two few-shot demonstrations are additional development examples, separate from these 100 evaluation variants.
Use autosomes only (chromosomes 1–22) throughout demonstrations, pilot queries, sensitivity checks, and fresh development validation. Exclude chromosome X before constructing any sampling pools.

Before selecting rows:

1. Verify the dataset's missense consequence label and select only missense groups.
2. Check eligible group counts and preserve complete groups.
3. Select deterministically with a recorded seed, without using model scores.
4. Record variant IDs, genomic build and coordinates, reference/alternate alleles, consequence labels, group IDs, source revision, and sequence checksums.
5. Verify reference alleles against the genome and extract centered 255-base windows: 127 bases on either side of the SNV.
6. Prepare both forward and reverse-complement inputs, transforming allele and position descriptions consistently.

Use the same pilot variants for every approach.
Draw few-shot examples from a separate part of the development split, excluding pilot groups, duplicate variants, and overlapping windows.
Prefer chromosome-disjoint example/query pools where the available missense groups permit it; record the actual separation used.
Do not use the held-out test split for prompt selection or development evaluation.

### Approaches to compare

Let `L_c(s)` be the sum of log probabilities of the DNA tokens in sequence `s`, conditional on prefix `c`.
Exclude the prefix itself and any EOS probability from this score.
For reference/alternate contrasts, retain identical conditioning text and use summed likelihoods rather than means over variable numbers of BPE tokens.
Define token-boundary handling explicitly before execution.

#### Template conventions

The following templates define the current v3 comparison. Historical v1/v2 templates and results remain archived at their original commits.

- Replace `{sequence}` with either the reference or alternate 255-base window, in separate requests.
- DNA is uppercase, on one line, with no spaces.
- Likelihood inputs have no trailing newline; classification FASTA records have a newline before their closing code fence.
- `{reference_sequence}` is the complete reference window for a classification query; its alternate allele is specified by the compact VCF row.
- `{ref_base}` and `{alt_base}` are the alleles in the displayed orientation.
- Position 128 is 1-based within the displayed 255-base window, including after reverse complementation.
- Braces denote substitution placeholders and are not sent literally.
- Newlines shown inside templates are literal.
- Outer four-backtick fences delimit the classification templates; the inner FASTA/VCF three-backtick fences are literal model input.
- VCF columns are separated by literal tabs; each record uses synthetic contig `sequence` and local coordinates.
- No gene name, genomic coordinate, consequence category, or true query label is included in the query text.

#### 1. Unprompted sequence likelihood

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
{sequence}
```

There is no text before the DNA and no trailing newline.
Score all DNA tokens, excluding any BOS or EOS target.
Score `L_empty(ref) - L_empty(alt)` on each strand and average.
This is the basic Hero VEP baseline.

#### 2. Healthy-individual prefix

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
The following sequence is from a healthy individual:
{sequence}
```

The prefix ends in exactly one newline after the colon.
There is no trailing newline after the DNA.
Score only the DNA continuation, excluding the sentence and its newline.
Verify that tokenization permits this scoring boundary; do not silently include a token spanning prefix text and DNA in the DNA-only score.

Score `L_healthy(ref) - L_healthy(alt)` on each strand and average.
The likelihood comparison has exactly two prefix conditions: no text prefix and this healthy-individual prefix.

#### 3. Zero-shot classification (v3)

Use one fixed, seeded answer mapping per variant, shared across zero-shot, two-shot and both strands. Seed 11181 ranks variant identities by SHA-256, independently of labels; each panel is split exactly in half between A=pathogenic/B=benign and A=benign/B=pathogenic. The [mapping manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/answer-mappings-v2.json) records all assignments: 50/50 for the pilot and 150/150 for validation.

In both templates, substitute `{class_A}`/`{class_B}` with the assigned labels. The final query prompt ends exactly at `Answer:` with no trailing space or newline. Candidate completions are ` A` and ` B`, including their leading space. Demonstrated answers retain the same visible `Answer: A` / `Answer: B` format.

````text
Classify single-nucleotide variants for Mendelian disease.
Each FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
Each compact VCF describes one substitution in its accompanying sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to that sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.
A: {class_A}
B: {class_B}
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Query:
```fasta
>sequence
{reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{ref_base}	{alt_base}
```
Which classification applies to variant V01 in the query?
Answer:
````

Tokenize the complete prefix-plus-candidate and require an unchanged prefix followed by exactly one answer token. On the tested tokenizer, ` A`=362 and ` B`=426. Request both IDs in one unmasked next-token response (`logprob_token_ids`, `max_tokens=1`); ignore the sampled token. Small live parity checks matched separate teacher-forced scores exactly. Never force a standalone-space token followed by bare A/B.

Compute `log P(pathogenic letter) - log P(benign letter)` under the assigned mapping and average the two strands. There is one benchmark score per method, not a mapping-average score. Both-mapping checks belong only in a small separate diagnostic subset.

#### 4. Two-shot classification (v3)

Insert exactly the two fixed labeled demonstrations into the same template. Their answer letters follow the query's assigned mapping. Instructions, option placement, query bytes and answer suffix remain identical to zero-shot; removing only the example section produces the zero-shot prompt byte-for-byte.

````text
Classify single-nucleotide variants for Mendelian disease.
Each FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
Each compact VCF describes one substitution in its accompanying sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to that sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.
A: {class_A}
B: {class_B}
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Example 1:
```fasta
>sequence
{example_1_reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{example_1_ref_base}	{example_1_alt_base}
```
Answer: {example_1_letter}

Example 2:
```fasta
>sequence
{example_2_reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{example_2_ref_base}	{example_2_alt_base}
```
Answer: {example_2_letter}

Query:
```fasta
>sequence
{reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{ref_base}	{alt_base}
```
Which classification applies to variant V01 in the query?
Answer:
````

The same leading-space single-token scoring rule applies. Use forward and reverse-complement query/example sequences with correctly transformed alleles; the centered position stays 128 and the biological labels stay unchanged. Reuse the same variant mapping on both strands. The benchmark has 16 scores per variant: eight DNA and eight classification scores, halving the earlier classification work. The old explicit-pair input-format check is not part of the v3 benchmark. Each A/B pair shares one response: 400 classification scoring responses for 100 variants, plus monitoring. The 800 historical DNA scores are reused with input-hash, serving-identity and sentinel checks.

### Shared-prefix caching and tokenization

Rely on vLLM's automatic prefix caching when enabled and supported by the scoring request path; do not implement a separate client-side KV cache.
For a centered SNV, the reference and alternate share the left flank:

```text
reference = left flank + reference allele + right flank
alternate = left flank + alternate allele + right flank
```

The shared prefix's likelihood cancels in the reference/alternate difference.
Both the variant and downstream sequence must still be scored: identical downstream letters have different conditioning histories after the mutation.
Cache reuse operates on identical token prefixes, so a base-level mutation can also change the boundary of the reusable token prefix.

The distinction to verify is between normal next-token scoring and requesting log probabilities for tokens already in the prompt:

- **A/B classification:** prefer obtaining both candidate probabilities from the next-token distribution without asking for all prompt logprobs, if the endpoint supports it.
  Repeated few-shot demonstrations can then benefit from the server's normal prefix caching.
- **DNA likelihood:** the straightforward `echo`/prompt-logprob route requests scores throughout the input.
  The current vLLM V1 guide states that such requests bypass prefix-cache reads and recompute the prompt, even with prefix caching enabled.
  Verify the deployed build's behavior rather than assuming the shared half is reused.

Before the pilot, verify tokenization and scoring boundaries and check available cache metrics for the actual request path.
Use server-managed reuse where available; a correct uncached baseline is acceptable for this 100-variant pilot, with its runtime recorded.
Consider a supported selective-scoring interface only if necessary for subsequent scaling, and validate score parity before adoption.

### Execution and completion criteria

1. **Prepare inputs and scoring definitions.**
   Verify missense membership, freeze the 100-variant sample and two-demonstration manifests, and save exact prompt templates.
2. **Validate a few pairs.**
   Inspect sequence construction, token boundaries, score signs, both strands, and actual caching behavior; check parity if using a selective-scoring path.
3. **Run the small development pilot.**
   Apply all four approaches to the same subset with bounded concurrency, request limits, and a recorded endpoint-use budget.
   Confirm these execution limits before launch; this draft does not launch a sweep or provision compute.
4. **Inspect and iterate.**
   Save per-variant reference/alternate likelihoods, classification scores, strand disagreement, prompt sensitivity, errors, latency, and token/cache accounting.
   Inspect within-group pathogenic-versus-control ranking and representative failure cases.
   AUPRC on ten positives is exploratory; the pilot does not meet the existing evaluator's 30-group threshold for standard per-subset reporting.
5. **Freeze and validate more broadly.**
   Freeze templates, demonstrations, score formulas, and selection rules before evaluating a fresh, larger development subset.
   Use established consequence-stratified metrics and paired match-group resampling to compare methods where sample size supports it.

Preserve raw scoring outputs and request metadata so scores can be recomputed without rerunning inference.
Keep pilot tuning results distinct from the later frozen-method validation results.
Do not describe this pilot as clinical validation or as an official benchmark result.

### Open decisions

- The fixed-rank, sequential workaround passed the complete pilot. Deployment-wide batch invariance remains unvalidated; retain stability guards for continuation.
- Plain-completion templates and contextual A/B tokenization passed live checks. A native chat-template comparison remains a possible later experiment.
- Measured smoke requests showed no prefix-cache queries or hits; use uncached accounting unless a different route is verified.
- The paced trial supersedes the four-client execution proposal. Use one fixed rank, one request in flight, a one-second completion gap, and sentinel/latency stops for continuation. The completed v3 rerun used caps of 2,000 HTTP requests and 30 minutes; it finished within both caps.
- V3 supersedes the earlier freezes. Its corrected pilot is complete; review it before fresh validation. The main benchmark uses one assigned mapping; both-mapping diagnostics remain separate. Longer-context experiments remain subsequent work.

The initial prompt bytes, demonstration split, and seed are now recorded in the research archive; they are no longer unspecified preparation tasks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether Marin Hero ranks pathogenic missense variants above matched common controls using sequence likelihood alone, and whether healthy-individual conditioning or labeled demonstrations improve those rankings.
Compare all four approaches on the same 100 variants, preserving forward/reverse-complement scores and matched groups.
The pilot can expose scoring failures and prompt sensitivity; ten positive variants are insufficient for a reliable benchmark claim.

## Status

As of November 13, 2026, the corrected v3 pilot is complete. Source `1774527a7557b7a8f7fa665c9b006b557ef10735` ran 400 fresh classification responses plus 72 monitoring responses in 11m29s. All 1,757 HTTP requests succeeded; all 108 sentinel observations had zero drift. All 800 reused DNA target scores passed provenance checks, and their aggregates reproduce v1 exactly. Maximum completion latency was 0.998 seconds. No serving settings changed. These checks do not measure other users' latency.

| Current v3 method | AUPRC | Bootstrap SE | Within-group pairwise wins |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Null DNA prefix (reused) | 0.213 | 0.045 | 63.3% |
| Healthy prefix (reused) | 0.302 | 0.093 | 64.4% |
| Zero-shot | 0.110 | 0.037 | 48.9% |
| Two-shot | 0.101 | 0.034 | 40.6% |

Two-shot minus zero-shot is -0.008 (95% bootstrap interval -0.065 to +0.036). Ten matched groups remain exploratory. Historical v1 classification selected under these same v3 mappings scored 0.185 zero-shot and 0.098 two-shot; the older all-primary headline scores below are not a mapping-controlled comparison. No score signs were flipped. [Completed v3 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-report.md), [metrics](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-metrics.json), [per-variant scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-variants.json), and [replayable target scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-scores.jsonl).

V2's token-alignment smoke passed, but subsequent EOS diagnostics invalidated its standalone-space remedy. V3 is the current protocol; no full v2 run occurred. The 300-variant development validation remains unrun. Durable batch-invariant shared serving remains unvalidated.

### Completed v1 pilot: historical exploratory results

Ten autosomal missense match groups contain ten pathogenic variants and 90 controls. Scores average both strands. Standard errors use 2,000 match-group bootstrap resamples, seed 11181, with the pinned MarinDNA evaluator. Ten groups are below its 30-group threshold for standard subset reporting.

| Method | AUPRC | Bootstrap SE | Pathogenic-versus-control pairwise wins |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Null DNA prefix | 0.213 | 0.045 | 63.3% |
| Healthy-individual prefix | 0.302 | 0.093 | 64.4% |
| Zero-shot classification | 0.068 | 0.011 | 21.1% |
| Two-shot classification | 0.263 | 0.088 | 71.7% |
| Zero-shot, mapping average (secondary) | 0.094 | 0.028 | 35.6% |
| Two-shot, mapping average (secondary) | 0.114 | 0.029 | 52.8% |

The healthy-minus-null AUPRC difference is +0.089, with paired bootstrap interval −0.044 to +0.220; this pilot does not establish a reliable conditioning benefit. Classification depends strongly on the letter assignment: swapping A/B flips score signs in 94/100 zero-shot and 76/100 two-shot cases, and reverses 50/90 and 36/90 strict positive-control pair orders. These comparisons already use pathogenic-minus-benign scores under each mapping; no sign correction is missing. The primary two-shot advantage should not be treated as mapping-robust.

The run completed all 2,448 targets in 66m17s, with 6,285 HTTP requests, all successful, under the 10,000-request/90-minute cap. All 306 sentinel repeats and 248 targets shared with the preceding paced trial matched exactly. Completion latency excluding pacing was 0.395 seconds median, 0.635 seconds p95, and 0.974 seconds maximum. One client, a fixed rank, and one-second completion gaps limited our traffic; these measurements do not establish isolated capacity or measure other users' latency. No cache savings or deployment changes are claimed.

[Report and representative failures](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-report.md), [metrics and paired uncertainty](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-100-metrics.json), [per-variant scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-100-variants.json), [strand/mapping/format sensitivity](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-100-sensitivity.json), [request and stability accounting](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-100-summary.json).

### Preparation and earlier diagnostic evidence

| Evidence | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned input selection | 493 eligible autosomal missense match groups; seed 11181 selects ten complete pilot groups (100 variants, ten positives), two chromosome-1 demonstrations, and 30 reserved validation groups (300 variants, 30 positives). Demonstrations and queries are chromosome-disjoint; pilot and validation windows do not overlap. [Manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/selected-variants.json), [selection summary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/preparation-result.json). |
| Sequence validation | Source/harness labels, central alleles, 255-base windows, reverse complements, and checksums passed. All 402 complete reference windows independently match Ensembl GRCh38. [Reference evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/ensembl-reference.summary.json), [raw public responses](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/ensembl-reference.jsonl). |
| Implementation | Exact templates, bounded scoring requests, per-request replay evidence, complete-matrix aggregation, strand/mapping sensitivity, and native MarinDNA matched-group metrics are implemented in the research archive. Ten offline tests and lint pass. Live protocol checks pass; the complete paced pilot supports the guarded workaround, while general batch invariance remains unvalidated. [Source and notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md). |
| Metric verification | Synthetic 10- and 30-group fixtures verify AP=1 for perfect rankings, zero paired deltas for identical methods, and the 30-group standard-reporting threshold. These are software checks, not model scores. [Validation record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/metrics-validation.json). |
| Dataset inference | Two completed ten-variant smoke runs (272 scores each) passed complete-matrix checks, but rankings changed across repeats for all four methods. These earlier smoke runs motivated the guarded policy; completed full-pilot results are reported above. Validation remains unrun. [Repeat comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/23d0ef3402913f1659797dda8aa9a28ef48f8a05/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/smoke-repeat-comparison.json). |
| Earlier unpinned sequential repeatability | Eight identical payloads replayed three times each also varied: target-only ranges 0.0445–0.6876 log-probability units. [Target scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/23d0ef3402913f1659797dda8aa9a28ef48f8a05/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/sequential-stability.json). |
| Prefix caching | Sequential smoke processed 91,512 prompt tokens; measured prefix-cache queries and hits both remained zero. No cache savings established. |

### Historical endpoint feasibility check

On November 6, 2026, an authenticated Hero service returned HTTP 200 for `ACGTACGTACGTACGT` through `/v1/completions` with `echo: true`, `logprobs: 1`, and `max_tokens: 0`. All eight DNA tokens received finite log probabilities, summing to `-25.680376634001732`, conditional on BOS and excluding EOS. Usage reported one internal completion token although the returned text contained only the input. The scorer accepts this accounting behavior while checking that echoed token IDs exactly match the input.

This proves likelihood access on that service at that time. It does not prove current availability, correct variant rankings, or prefix-cache reuse.

### Current serving evidence

On November 13, an authenticated final SFT step-400407 service passed model discovery, tokenization, and echoed prompt-logprob scoring. The user approved proceeding on this checkpoint, replacing the earlier quick-SFT probe model. Both contextual answer continuations are single tokens. Exact service URLs, deployment identifiers, authentication instructions, and private discussion links remain outside this issue.

Sequential and four-client smoke runs used identical input hashes, token IDs, and scoring boundaries. Native and echoed observed-token logprobs agree exactly, and one serving fingerprint was observed across the 544 completed smoke responses. Yet maximum strand-averaged score differences were 2.8781 (null), 0.5401 (healthy), 0.8898 (zero-shot), and 0.2611 (two-shot), changing all four rankings. Sequential replay also varied, so our concurrency alone does not explain the problem. Subsequent controlled probes isolated rank and batch dependence, as detailed below; the exact numerical kernel remains unidentified. No serving configuration was changed.

An earlier parallel attempt ended with SIGTERM after 223 scores; its partial evidence is preserved separately and excluded from the completed comparisons. [Published notebook and evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/23d0ef3402913f1659797dda8aa9a28ef48f8a05/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).

### Rank and batching diagnosis (November 13)

The service uses unquantized BF16 with data/expert parallelism. The supported `X-data-parallel-rank` header isolated two effects:

- Across four selected ranks, two fixed prompts repeated three times each were exactly stable within each rank but differed between ranks (24 completions).
- On fixed rank 0, all 36 targets covering two autosomal variants, both strands, all four methods and an explicit-pair format check matched exactly across two sequential passes. A four-client pass changed the same targets, by up to 5.6548 DNA log-likelihood units and 0.6612 classification-token log-probability units (108 completions total).
- A final sequential pass after concurrent traffic recovered all 36 original scores exactly.

**Bounded workaround:** pin one rank and serialize calls, with repeated sentinels. This worked in these checks but other traffic on a shared expert-parallel service can still affect batching. Repeatability is distinct from model correctness.

**Durable fix to test:** `serve.vllm_batch_invariant: true` on an approved scoring service, followed by rank/batch/order repeatability checks and performance measurement. Hero/GrugMoE is not among the deployed version's documented validated models; the flag is not a verified fix yet. Preserve compilation and CUDA graphs. If it fails, compare replicated parameter hashes and intermediate activations across ranks to localize the kernel/reduction. The newer serving release's documented fixes do not establish a fix for this BF16 prefill discrepancy.

[Controlled evidence, exact scores and next diagnostic steps](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0a85603e147815c1a809f82ae7ae8c691e7b20c8/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md). Endpoint and access details remain private. No deployment or restart was performed. At that diagnostic stage, neither full pilot nor validation had run; the subsequent completed pilot is reported above.

### Paced shared-endpoint trial (November 13)

The user-approved ten-variant trial completed in **7m38s** on fixed rank 0 with one request in flight and a minimum one-second gap between completion requests. All 706 HTTP requests succeeded. The complete matrix contains 272 panel scores plus six sentinel baselines and 36 sentinel repeats. **Every repeat matched exactly**, and all 36 overlapping targets from the earlier fixed-rank sequential diagnostic also matched.

Completion latency excluding pauses: median 0.408 seconds, p95 0.649 seconds, maximum 0.941 seconds. No drift, failure, or latency stop triggered. The trial averaged 0.686 completion calls/second including pauses and setup and processed 105,911 prompt tokens. This limits our traffic; it does not measure other users' latency or establish isolated GPU capacity.

[Trial accounting and checks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c316640755e3cba1b428e9b35371d811c9bb7a3d/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/paced-trial-summary.json), [sentinel evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c316640755e3cba1b428e9b35371d811c9bb7a3d/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/paced-trial-sentinels.json), [guarded runner](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c316640755e3cba1b428e9b35371d811c9bb7a3d/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/paced.py). Retain rank pinning, serialization, pacing, and repeat/latency stop conditions for any continuation. This ten-variant gate preceded the completed full pilot reported above. Reserved validation remains unrun; no deployment or serving settings changed.

### Remaining work and Loom feedback

[Loom's proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11181#issuecomment-6778568972) informed the experimental harness: pinned manifests, reference checks, scoring, aggregation, exact prompts, and offline tests are implemented. Ten focused tests and saved-response replay passed, and the harness passed CI. The research branch preserves the experiment history. These artifacts support this experiment; promoting them into `main` is explicitly outside this issue's scope. The previously opened harness and archive-index PRs are closed without merging.

1. The fixed-rank, sequential, paced ten-variant gate passed. Retain sentinel and latency stops when continuing; shared-service batch invariance remains a separate validation task. No new GPU deployment has been provisioned.
2. Preserve the passed live checks for BOS handling, DNA boundaries, both contextual A/B probabilities, complete matrices, latency, and cache accounting. Repeat the stability gate after any serving change.
3. V1 and v3 pilots are separately archived. V3 execution and canonical answer tokenization passed, but classification remains weak. Next compare general language models, beginning with GLM-5.3 null/healthy likelihood scoring after compatibility checks; no DNA-specialist peers.
4. Validate the revised protocol on the reserved 300-variant development panel only after the v3 pilot review. Record an updated endpoint-use budget for its smaller 4,800-target matrix. Keep one client, pacing and stability guards; keep the held-out test split untouched. Validation remains unlaunched.
5. Finish the experiment report and preserve reproducible code, results, and conclusions on the branches. Keep the issue open until the experimental evidence supports its conclusion. No PR or merge into `main` is required or planned.

## Links

- [Current v3 protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/protocol-v3.md), [Completed v3 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-report.md), and [current notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/0ae6c758a4f33c220c3938a62c969ec47ba51593/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).

- [Historical, superseded v2 protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/protocol-v2.md), [mapping assignments](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/answer-mappings-v2.json), [exact rendered prompt examples](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/prompt-examples-v2.json), and [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c66cf85742e51f037e921993d0b7eda3aff46b3b/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).

- [Completed pilot report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-report.md) and [current research notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f7592176b0bb20b25509ef9019ecf4f6163894b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).

- [Experimental harness branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/11181-vep-harness). [PR #11375](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11375) is closed, unmerged.
- [Research branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/codex/11181-hero-vep).
- [Archive index branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/codex/11181-vep-index); [PR #41](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/pull/41) is closed, unmerged.

- [Research notebook, source, and validation evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).
- W&B Report: not created.
- Important updates: v3 pilot complete and analyzed; v2 standalone-space remedy rejected; fresh validation unrun. See Status above.

- [Mendelian dataset at the pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-dna/evals_mendelian_traits/tree/4aed58e50c5dea0b878a665007af2ef9e5108e9f)

- [Pinned evaluation configuration](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/config/config.yaml)
- [Shared-prefix scoring kernel](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/src/marin_dna_evals/model/scoring.py)
- [LLR harness and strand aggregation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/src/marin_dna_evals/lm_eval/dna_vep_llr_eval.py)
- [Dataset descriptions](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/dashboard/src/data/datasets.json.py)
- [vLLM automatic prefix caching](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/automatic_prefix_caching/)
- [vLLM V1 prompt-logprob behavior](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/v1_guide/#prompt-logprobs-with-prefix-caching)
- [Newer selective prompt scoring documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs/)
- [VEP-bench FASTA/VCF prompt representation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/205df32032b9ff6be11bc387879e8bed578839aa/configs/tasks/sge/prompt.yaml)


## Decision Log

- November 13 (v3): canonical leading-space answer tokens, one joint response per A/B pair, same seeded mappings and shared template. Complete pilot: AUPRC 0.110 zero-shot and 0.101 two-shot. No post-hoc sign flips. General-language-model peers only; prioritize likelihood scoring.
- November 13 (v2, superseded after EOS diagnosis): condition on the trailing space and score bare A/B; use one seeded balanced mapping per variant; use an identical zero-/two-shot template except for demonstrations. Implemented and smoke-verified; supersedes the v1 freeze. Preserve v1 results separately.

- November 13: freeze all four original primary methods, score signs, templates, demonstrations and both-strand averages after pilot analysis. Keep mapping averages secondary; do not select a mapping or flip score signs to improve pilot performance.

- November 13: keep this work as a branch-based experiment. Contributions or merges into `main` are out of scope; both PRs are closed with branches preserved.

- November 13: proceed on the available final Hero SFT step-400407 checkpoint, replacing the earlier quick-SFT feasibility model. Preserve the checkpoint distinction in all results.
- Use 100 missense variants: ten complete match groups, with ten positives and 90 controls.
- Compare exactly two DNA-likelihood prefixes: no text prefix and the healthy-individual sentence.
- Use FASTA/VCF classification inputs with synthetic contig `sequence`, A/B answer likelihoods, and a reversed-label sensitivity check.
- Use only autosomes throughout. Reserve chromosome 1 for two separate missense demonstrations, one pathogenic and one control; query groups use other autosomes. Fix selection and demonstration order with seed 11181.
- Reserve 30 complete fresh development groups (300 variants) for validation after freezing the protocol. Exclude pilot overlaps and keep the held-out test split unused.
- Rely on server-managed prefix caching where supported; verify the scoring request path and allow an uncached pilot baseline.
- Keep service URLs, deployment identifiers, and access instructions outside the public issue.

## Conclusion

V3 corrects the answer-token boundary and confirms stable execution, but classification remains weak: AUPRC 0.110 zero-shot and 0.101 two-shot. DNA likelihood remains the more promising direction in this exploratory ten-group pilot; the healthy-prefix benefit is still uncertain. Prioritize a general-language-model comparison, starting with GLM-5.3 likelihood compatibility. DNA-specialist peers are out of scope. Reserved validation remains unrun. This is a branch-based experiment; production integration and merging into `main` remain out of scope.

🤖
# Research

The issue is a multi-session experiment: the short endpoint check established prompt log probabilities, but no missense manifest, paired variant scores, or classification results exist yet. The checkout has served completion evaluation code, but no VEP evaluator; the existing DNA training prefix is different from the two likelihood conditions specified here. I found no open PR for #11181 or VEP.

**Relevant code**
- [`client.py#L72-L112`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L72-L112) — served completion scoring route.
- [`dna.py#L120-L126`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/dna.py#L120-L126) — existing DNA training prefix.

# Proposed Fix

1. Create the research logbook and a pinned input manifest. Inspect the dataset's missense label and eligible group counts, select ten complete groups plus two disjoint demonstrations with a recorded seed, and verify the reference genome, alleles, 255-base windows, reverse complements, and checksums.
2. Add a small VEP harness under `experiments/evals/` with offline behavior tests. Freeze exact prompt bytes and score formulas; verify DNA token boundaries and both A/B candidate probabilities in context. Persist per-request token scores and metadata so every aggregate can be recomputed.
3. Validate a few pairs against the deployed checkpoint and tokenizer. Record score signs, strand behavior, latency, and whether the actual scoring requests use prefix caching. Set request count, concurrency, and wall-time limits with endpoint users before running all 100 variants.

2. Fix the failing sync operation and make the peer sync loop survive transient exceptions while logging them. Keep the cursor unchanged when a batch fails so the next pass retries it.
3. Add a regression that drives the failure and recovery through serialized federation deltas, then verifies the hub mirrors terminal parent and child states.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
The curated evaluation driver keeps far fewer generation requests in flight than its configured concurrency of 64, so generation evals run several times slower than the model allows. Two 1,000-item SimpleQA Verified runs on CoreWeave H100s, with the judge on Together:

| Run | Median model latency | Mean requests in flight | Eval time | Time if 64 were in flight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qwen3.6-35b-a3b, thinking off | 2.0 s | 5.0 | 9.1 min | 0.7 min |
| gpt-oss-20b, thinking on | 11.5 s | 25.4 | 9.2 min | 3.7 min |

Timings come from the orchestrator's `InferenceProxy submitted request` and `returning response` log lines. Both runs take about 9 minutes whatever the model's speed, roughly 0.55 s per item. The same evals through vendored Evalchemy, also at concurrency 64, took 2.1 and 5.9 minutes.

Likely cause: each consumer in `lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py` makes two synchronous FineStore transactions per item:
- the `STARTED` attempt row, at `evaluation.py:714`;
- `_save_attempt`, at `evaluation.py:287`.

Each transaction writes shards and a blob to S3, then commits the manifest under `_commit_lock` (`lib/finestore/src/finestore/store.py:365`). Background compaction also takes that lock. Because the transactions run on the event-loop thread, each commit pauses all 64 consumers. The judge call already runs in `asyncio.to_thread`. I have not timed a single transaction.

Reproduce:
1. With #11063, run `uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model-config experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/model-configs/Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.yaml --evals simpleqa-verified --priority batch`.
2. From the orchestrator's `InferenceProxy` log lines, compute the requests in flight over time.

Expected: requests in flight stay close to the configured concurrency while work is queued, and eval time approaches the model-bound time.

Runs, under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`: `sqav-v3-full-qwen36-20261113-simpleqa-verified-fd86639097f450a697aea50c48e31ca3` and `sqav-v3-full-gptoss-20261113-simpleqa-verified-thinking-21ac6ebf1d6b5eff9fec1f8174444bc1`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`produce()` commits selection rows on the event loop before dispatching each eligible case; `consume()` commits the `STARTED` row there, and `_score_generation()` / `_score_likelihood()` commit terminal evidence there. FineStore serializes commits under `_commit_lock`, so S3 writes and compaction can stall every coroutine even when model concurrency is 64.

**Relevant code**
- [`evaluation.py#L635-L689`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L635-L689) - per-case selection commits
- [`evaluation.py#L695-L717`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L695-L717) - start commits
- [`evaluation.py#L287-L315`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L287-L315) - terminal evidence commits
- [`store.py#L365-L381`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finestore/src/finestore/store.py#L365-L381) - serialized transaction commit

# Proposed Fix

Await each selection, start, and terminal transaction through `asyncio.to_thread()`. Keep selection commits ahead of queue dispatch and terminal commits ahead of completion, then test event-loop responsiveness and the persisted selection/attempt rows on simulated storage.

```
File "/tests/prepare.py", line 15, in main

FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/answer.txt'
```

comments.body:

# Research

[Incident #982](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/982) traces `TransferBudgetExceeded` to a cross-region bundle read during handoff. On current `main`, the exception escapes `_deliver_handoff()` and `future.result()`, ending that peer's sync thread. A read-only hub query at 19:52 UTC still found 114 pending, unacknowledged handoffs for `cw-us-east-02a` and 11 for `cw-us-east-08a`; a 19:51 thread dump showed both heartbeat threads but neither sync thread ([incident #984](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/984)). Why the hub consumed its 10 GB cross-region budget remains unknown.

**Relevant code**
- [`manager.py#L385-L401`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/acd9b1193678436b3c6b714b06f297ace586c50c/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/manager.py#L385-L401) — handoff futures propagate exceptions
- [`manager.py#L409-L446`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/acd9b1193678436b3c6b714b06f297ace586c50c/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/manager.py#L409-L446) — bundle-read exception is uncaught

# Proposed Fix

1. Catch `TransferBudgetExceeded` per handoff, preserve its pending handle, and log the job, peer, path, and budget. Test that a failed bundle read leaves the peer sync thread running and does not prevent another handoff or status sync.
2. Trace the hub's cross-region bundle reads and fix the storage placement or repeated reads that exhausted the process budget. Make budget-blocked handoffs visible in job status so operators can distinguish them from peer admission delays.
3. After review and operator approval for the named `marin` controller, deploy the fix and verify the existing 02a/08a handles advance to acceptance or an explicit recoverable error. Check the sync threads and pending counts without submitting duplicate jobs.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
TL;DR: The same Snowball checkpoint on the same vLLM serve gives different results for identical requests. Between two identical passes, the selected expert set changes at 5.55% of position-layers. One repeated request moved a summed log-prob by up to 0.62 nat on the baseline serve and 0.69 nat on the candidate serve. Over five passes of the rows used by the identity gate run after 16 SFT updates (below, "the gate"), the creator family mean moved by 0.091 nat/token, against a gate threshold of 0.10 nat/token. We do not know the cause. Part of #10695.

Setup: Snowball v0.1 (`adc0078a`) on the Marin vLLM fork at `01911be3`, BF16, DP8 with expert parallelism, FlashAttention 3. The gate receipts record sampling as `temperature=0.0`, `max_tokens=1` and `prompt_logprobs=0`.

Routes. A [route capture](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-vllm-route-capture-r1-reading-marten-md) ran the same 465 sequences twice on one serve, with `--enable-return-routed-experts` and eight requests in flight. Each pass covers 30,999 prompt positions over 26 MoE layers (805,974 position-layers). The [receipt](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-vllm-routes-r1-capture-receipt-json) records 761,213 matching top-4 expert sets. So 44,761 position-layers (5.55%) flip. Ordered top-4 agreement is 88.24%. Agreement is 99.95% at layer 0 (16 of 30,999 positions flip, 0.05%) and falls to 90.57% at layer 12. Prefix-cache hits were 0 in both passes. Capture and the eight concurrent requests can change scheduling, so this is not a one-in-flight measurement.

Log-probs. The gate's [baseline receipt](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-baseline-json) records `logprob_stability_max_abs_diff` for three repeated rows: 0.619, 0.451 and 0.210 nat. The [candidate receipt](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-candidate-json) records 0.566, 0.687 and 0.244 nat for the same three rows. Each run sent one request at a time to a serve used only by the gate. The DP8+EP collectives still run across all ranks.

Family means. The same receipt scores the 24 primary rows in five passes. The range of the family mean NLL across passes is 0.053 nat/token for name rows and 0.091 nat/token for creator rows. On the candidate serve the ranges are 0.036 (name) and 0.0018 (creator) nat/token ([decision](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)). The gate decides on a 0.10 nat/token improvement. An earlier three-pass baseline gave 0.041 (name) and 0.053 (creator), per-row spread median 0.092 and max 0.425, and 0.019-0.023 between two serves of the same model ([noise amendment](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-milestone16-spending-gate-a1-md)).

Torch reference. The torch eager reference is deterministic at batch 1: a rerun reproduces every route ([torch floor](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-torch-floor-r1-reading-chukar-md)). It is sensitive to batch shape. With the gate's grids (batch 8, right-pad 64, mask), set agreement with its own batch-1 routes is 94.65% overall, 98.29% at layer 0 and 90.72% at layer 20. Torch batched against vLLM at layer 0 is 95.85% (pass 1) and 95.83% (pass 2) ([batched floor](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-flag-arms-r1-batched-floor-json)). A [layer-0 route amendment](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-precision-preflight-amendment-g1b-shoveler-md) to the precision gate uses that value as the layer-0 floor. Served attention also differs from the torch reference in rounding order, softmax scaling and RoPE precision ([source read](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-attention-backends-and-rounding-marten-md)). So torch is an imperfect reference for this noise.

Impact. A comparison of two vLLM-scored checkpoints has noise from both serves. With three passes, the noise amendment estimated the pooled two-checkpoint creator spread at about 0.07 nat/token. With five passes per checkpoint, the decision file records a pooled spread of 0.064 (name) and 0.091 (creator) nat/token. Both are most of the 0.10 threshold. A single-pass win or loss near the threshold can come from serve noise alone. The 5.55% repeat flip rate applies to comparisons over all layers. The layer-0 route check compares layer 0 only, where the repeat flip rate is 0.05%.

Mitigation in place. The [noise amendment](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-milestone16-spending-gate-a1-md) keeps the gate's first-pass decision. Each checkpoint scores the 24 primary rows five times. The result is labelled INCONCLUSIVE if `too_weak` differs between any pair of pass-wise evaluations, or if |first-pass improvement - 0.10| is smaller than sqrt(range_base^2 + range_cand^2) for the deciding family. An INCONCLUSIVE result authorizes no continuation and no pass claim. The baseline receipt above records the amendment's file hash.

Cause: unknown. We have not tested whether the variation comes from batch composition, DP/EP collective order, or kernel choice. The log-prob runs sent one request at a time and still vary. We infer from this that batching of scoring requests with each other does not explain the log-prob variation. We have not tested it directly.

Done when: the source of the run-to-run variation is identified, or a serve configuration gives bit-identical log-probs for identical requests, or the noise floor is measured and documented for each eval that compares vLLM-scored checkpoints.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 This is a serving investigation, not yet a scoped code fix. [#7554](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7554) found cross-rank variation from BF16 expert-parallel reduction and a residual local-path effect on an earlier fork; same-rank recomputes were bit-identical in that setup. The #10699 receipts do not establish DP rank for each repeated request, so rank placement remains a live explanation. The existing [Snowball parity harness](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/tests/cluster/vllm/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L390-L415) already pins ranks and checks same-rank repeats.

Plan:
1. Replay the pinned Snowball checkpoint and fork `01911be3` on one serve. Use the 24 gate rows and three stability rows as fixed token IDs. Record request-to-DP-rank mapping, batch/prefill shape, cache hits, top-4 routes, and prompt log-probs over five serial passes and five eight-in-flight passes; repeat after a cold launch. Report layer-wise route agreement, per-row log-prob spread, and family-mean NLL ranges against the existing receipts.
2. If rank-pinned repeats differ, trace one flipping row through the first divergent layer: attention output, router logits/top-4, expert output, and post-combine tensor. Reuse the boundary approach from #7554. Change one factor at a time (request scheduling, attention backend, then expert-combine order/precision) while keeping weights and token IDs fixed.
3. If a serving operation is responsible, patch the Marin vLLM fork and add rank-pinned serial and concurrent repeat regressions. Re-run the five-pass gate before claiming the 0.10 nat/token decision is stable. If no deterministic configuration emerges, publish the measured repeat spread for each vLLM-scored eval and retain the A1 `INCONCLUSIVE` rule near the threshold.

The first experiment decides whether this is rank placement, within-rank execution, or both; a PR can then target the measured cause.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 On a four-H100 serve of Snowball v0.1's weights (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` at `6783e974`, the same files as v0.1 at your `adc0078a` except the model card, on marin-community/vllm@e09cfd55, DP4 with expert parallelism, prefix caching off), repeated identical scoring requests (`max_tokens` 1, temperature 0, `prompt_logprobs` 0) gave bit-identical log-probs, the same on all four ranks, in fresh launches and next to other traffic, with four settings:

- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.
- A fixed-root reduction of the expert outputs, which 01911be3 does under batch invariance ([`cuda_communicator.py#L525-L531`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py#L525-L531)); we copied that code into e09cfd55.
- `--enforce-eager`, or `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1` with vLLM's combo-kernel benchmark off: `--compilation-config '{"inductor_compile_config": {"combo_kernels": true, "benchmark_combo_kernel": false}}'`. Deterministic mode alone stops the server at startup, since vLLM turns that benchmark on ([`compilation.py#L990-L1000`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/config/compilation.py#L990-L1000)). With the first two settings, scoring 256 requests took 38 s with the default compile, 38 to 44 s with the deterministic compile and 56 to 57 s eager.
- `--no-enable-chunked-prefill`, with `--max-num-batched-tokens` at least `--max-model-len`, when a rank prefills a prompt longer than one chunk next to other requests.

We measured four sources of mismatch in vLLM's default mode, and each setting above removed one:

- The rank that serves the request. With one request in flight, as in the gate, each unpinned repeat matched the pinned result of its rank (1,280 of 1,280). Pinned repeats (`X-data-parallel-rank` header) were bit-identical (512 of 512 pairs), and different ranks never matched (0 of 192; summed log-probs up to 22.7 nat apart, mean log-probs up to 0.138 nat/token). Without the header, the load balancer sends serial repeats to different ranks ([`core_client.py#L1556-L1591`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py#L1556-L1591) at 01911be3). With the fixed-root reduction, ranks that loaded the same cached compiled graph matched (192 of 192).
- Other requests on the same rank. Eight decode streams on the scored request's rank left 88 of 128 pairs identical, and on other ranks 128 of 128. Unpinned with eight scoring requests in flight, as in your route capture, 9 of 128 repeats were identical and 11.0% of position-layer route sets flipped (your capture: 5.55% on 465 shorter sequences, DP8 on 01911be3). Batch invariance removed the same-rank effect.
- Kernels that a fresh compile picks by timing at startup. Two launches with empty compile caches matched the first launch on 0 and 96 of 256 pairs, differing from layer 0 on. With batch invariance and the fixed-root reduction, two fresh compiles matched across ranks on only 114 and 73 of 192 pairs. Eager execution or the deterministic compile made three fresh launches each agree across ranks (192 of 192) and with one another (256 of 256).
- Prefill chunk boundaries, in the 19 of 26 layers that use the 2,048-token sliding window. With the first three settings, on 16 prompts of 8,000 to 17,000 tokens in 7,168-token chunks, eight decode streams on the same rank ended the first chunk up to 8 tokens earlier, and every prompt changed from its second chunk on (0 of 16 identical). Scored alone, chunks of 7,104 and 7,040 tokens, multiples of 32, reproduced the unchunked scores, and chunks of 7,000 did not. vLLM's FlashAttention 3 build, which your serve uses, starts each query tile's key range at its first query's window ([`block.h#L22-L33`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/block.h#L22-L33)); on this model a tile spans 32 positions.

On 01911be3, which has the fixed-root reduction, batch invariance plus eager execution or the deterministic compile should make the gate's one-at-a-time scores match on any rank and in any launch. The Snowball parity job sets `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` ([`test_snowball_backend_parity.py#L71`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_backend_parity.py#L71)) and scores one rank-pinned request per rank with prefix caching off ([`snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L324-L361`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L324-L361)) in [512-token chunks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L66), a multiple of 32. Its exact check is same-rank repeatability ([`#L441-L448`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L441-L448)); its cross-rank comparison is logged without an assertion ([`#L453-L461`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L453-L461)), and each case must match the goldens within a probability error of [0.125](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L78) ([`#L462-L465`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_backend_parity_jobs.py#L462-L465)). With the compile setting, the cross-rank comparison could be exact too.

marin-community/vllm#109 (open) fixes a different chunk-boundary dependence in vLLM's Triton attention backend. #10635 keeps chunked prefill in SkyRL's rollout engines by making each row past the window its own FlashAttention 3 request. Our serve is DP4 on e09cfd55 with torch 2.11, and yours is DP8 on 01911be3 with torch 2.13 ([`gpu.toml#L2-L5`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/41a41987e50e5ca68620f41c8714b1864c12f982/config/external/vllm/gpu.toml#L2-L5)). We have not run 01911be3.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` makes identical scoring requests bit-identical on the serve this issue describes (vLLM fork `01911be3`, DP8 with expert parallelism, torch 2.13, FlashAttention 3). That meets the second "Done when" condition, so I am closing the issue. The setting is an environment variable on the serving job.

**Gate requests on Snowball v0.1.** I served Snowball v0.1 (model revision `adc0078a`) with the gate's serve arguments plus `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, default compile. I scored the gate's 24 primary rows twice with the gate's own scorer (`identity_eval.py` at `2a1de41d`, `m16_gate.py` at `9e3857f8`). Each row scores several answer options, 206 in total, with one request per option. Requests went one at a time and were not pinned to a data-parallel rank, as in the original gate. "Original" below is `m16-gate-baseline.json`, the baseline receipt linked in the issue body.

| | Original | With batch invariance |
|---|---|---|
| Answer-option scores identical across passes | no | 206 of 206 |
| Largest change in a repeated row's summed log-prob | 0.619 nat | 0 |
| Range of the name family mean across passes | 0.053 nat/token (five passes) | 0 (two passes) |
| Range of the creator family mean across passes | 0.091 nat/token (five passes) | 0 (two passes) |

A family mean is the gate's statistic: the mean negative log-likelihood per token of the correct answer over the 14 name rows or the 10 creator rows. With batch invariance the name mean is 8.846 nat/token and the creator mean is 14.012. The original first pass gave 8.851 and 14.016. Both differences are inside the original's own range across passes.

**Ranks and launches.** I ran four launches of the same DP8 serve with batch invariance on the June 67B step-42150 export that the Snowball parity test uses. It is a different checkpoint from v0.1 with the same architecture and serve shape. Each launch compiled from an empty cache on a different node. Two used the default compile. Two used `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC=1` with `benchmark_combo_kernel` off, the setting from the comment above. Each launch scored 17 prompts of 31 to 15,025 tokens on every rank, pinned with `X-data-parallel-rank`, and compared every prompt position's log-prob exactly.

- Within each launch, all 8 ranks returned identical log-probs for all 17 prompts.
- Same-rank repeats matched on 136 of 136 (prompt, rank) pairs when sent serially, and on 136 of 136 with one request in flight on each rank.
- The two launches of each compile mode matched each other on 136 of 136 pairs.
- The two compile modes disagree with each other on all 136 pairs, by up to 0.0034 nat/token. Two serves must use the same compile mode before their scores are compared.

**Cause.** This part is inferred. The gate serve ran without batch invariance and sent unpinned requests, which the load balancer spreads over ranks. The comment above measured that ranks disagree in that mode and that a fixed-root reduction of expert outputs, which `01911be3` applies under batch invariance, removes the disagreement. My runs show the variation is gone with batch invariance. They do not separate rank placement from other sources, and I did not measure the default mode again.

**Limits.**

- I did not reproduce the fresh-compile mismatch that the comment above reports for `e09cfd55` with torch 2.11. On `01911be3` the default compile repeated across two fresh launches. Two launches cannot rule it out.
- The full gate was not rerun. It scores a baseline and a trained checkpoint, each on a 64-case grid and then five passes of the primary rows. The check above is the baseline only, primary rows only, two passes. It does not show that two serves of v0.1 agree with each other.
- No test put several requests in flight on one rank, so chunked prefill of a long prompt next to other traffic is untested.
- The comment above offers eager execution as an alternative to the deterministic compile. I did not test it.
- The gate check ran on `cw-us-east-02a`; the original gate ran on `cw-rno2a`.
- The gate loads `identity.jsonl` and `controls.jsonl`. `controls.jsonl` is not archived with the experiment, so an empty file stood in. It adds no scored case: the grid built from `identity.jsonl` alone has the same 64 cases as the original receipt, in rows, order, answer options and token spans.

**Using it.** `marin.inference.iris_cli` on main cannot set an environment variable on the serving job. The branch below adds `--env NAME=VALUE`. It is not merged and has no PR.

Code and results are on branch `worktree-vllm-10699-repeat-retest` at `da6495db`:

- [gate repeat driver](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da6495dba4c244d2fb30dd95f7fa748a45bb4010/experiments/post_training/identity_gate_batch_invariant.py) and its [result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da6495dba4c244d2fb30dd95f7fa748a45bb4010/experiments/post_training/issue_10699_results/gate-repeat-v0.1-batch-invariant.json)
- [rank repeat job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da6495dba4c244d2fb30dd95f7fa748a45bb4010/lib/marin/src/marin/testing/inference/snowball_repeat_determinism_jobs.py), its [launcher](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da6495dba4c244d2fb30dd95f7fa748a45bb4010/tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_repeat_determinism.py) and its [four results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/da6495dba4c244d2fb30dd95f7fa748a45bb4010/experiments/post_training/issue_10699_results)

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
Two full runs of the same frozen Snowball parent produced different coding scores, although their artifact model configs are equal and the Evalchemy config sets `seed: 42`.

| Benchmark | Run `2026.09.29.1` | Run `2026.09.29.7` | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| HumanEval+ | 51.83% | 42.07% | -9.76 points |
| MBPP+ | 42.06% | 44.18% | +2.12 points |
| CRUXEval input | 4.63% | 4.00% | -0.63 point |
| CRUXEval output | 8.88% | 7.63% | -1.25 points |

Both artifacts use:

- `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23@227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db`
- the same tokenizer revision
- an 8,192-token generation limit
- `skip_special_tokens=false` and `repetition_penalty=1.1`
- the same serving topology
- the `coding-expert-code` evaluation with seed 42 and thinking off

Artifacts:

- `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-python-expert-parent/coding-expert-code/2026.09.29.1`
- `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-python-expert-parent/coding-expert-code/2026.09.29.7`

The likely cause is that Evalchemy's launch seed does not set a fixed sampler seed for each OpenAI request. The code evaluation also has no explicit temperature, so the endpoint can use its sampling default. Confirm the request payload before selecting a fix.

One sampled answer per item can change enough to alter a model comparison. A recorded launch seed does not currently prove that a repeated generation run is deterministic.

This was found during #9528. Its temporary workaround is to run the frozen parent and candidate together, compare only that matched pair, and report paired task-level intervals. Do not compare the candidate to the earlier parent artifact. All four paired coding intervals in the matched run include zero, so the spike does not use the higher candidate point estimate as promotion evidence.

Done when:

1. Define the canonical sampler behavior for one-sample generation evaluations. Use an explicit deterministic temperature or derive and send a stable request seed from the task, document ID, and repeat index.
2. Store the effective request sampling values in the result provenance.
3. Add a repeatability check that runs the same small generated-task panel twice and compares the sample outputs.
4. Run the frozen parent twice after the fix and confirm equal outputs or document the expected variance when deterministic serving is not possible.

```markdown
| HumanEval+ | 51.83% | 42.07% | -9.76 points |
| MBPP+ | 42.06% | 44.18% | +2.12 points |
| CRUXEval input | 4.63% | 4.00% | -0.63 point |
| CRUXEval output | 8.88% | 7.63% | -1.25 points |

Both artifacts use:

- `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23@227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db`
- the same tokenizer revision
- an 8,192-token generation limit
- `skip_special_tokens=false` and `repetition_penalty=1.1`
- the same serving topology
- the `coding-expert-code` evaluation with seed 42 and thinking off

Artifacts:

- `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-python-expert-parent/coding-expert-code/2026.09.29.1`
- `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-python-expert-parent/coding-expert-code/2026.09.29.7`

The likely cause is that Evalchemy's launch seed does not set a fixed sampler seed for each OpenAI request. The code evaluation also has no explicit temperature, so the endpoint can use its sampling default. Confirm the request payload before selecting a fix.

## Impact

One sampled answer per item can change enough to alter a model comparison. A recorded launch seed does not currently prove that a repeated generation run is deterministic.

This was found during #9528. Its temporary workaround is to run the frozen parent and candidate together, compare only that matched pair, and report paired task-level intervals. Do not compare the candidate to the earlier parent artifact. All four paired coding intervals in the matched run include zero, so the spike does not use the higher candidate point estimate as promotion evidence.

## Proposed fix

1. Define the canonical sampler behavior for one-sample generation evaluations. Use an explicit deterministic temperature or derive and send a stable request seed from the task, document ID, and repeat index.
2. Store the effective request sampling values in the result provenance.
3. Add a repeatability check that runs the same small generated-task panel twice and compares the sample outputs.
4. Run the frozen parent twice after the fix and confirm equal outputs or document the expected variance when deterministic serving is not possible.

```
