spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Native SFTSpec Snowball d1024 training on one 8×H100 node passes forward evaluation but can hang in the first optimizer update. Every GPU reports 100% utilization, zero memory traffic and roughly 120–215W; Python rank main threads remain in XLA ExecuteReplicated. No completed update appears after more than five minutes. This blocks unmodified-runtime loss curves and throughput comparisons. d768 full-target training also stalled; d768 assistant-target and both d512 masks completed 20 updates.

Reproduce:
1. Load `open-athena/Snowflake-d1024-Base-262K-2026.10.19` at revision `dd3c5e3c156cfbe936fc0b59932c747e47c21d04` through native SFTSpec→TrainLmConfig→train_lm. Use sequence length 262144, global batch 8, microbatch 1, context parallel 4/data parallel 2, expert parallel 1, FP32 master parameters, BF16 computation, Sonic dispatch, gpu_fa4_cute attention, offloaded Muon-H optimizer and cuda_async allocator. The raw HF checkpoint evaluation and a second evaluation after resetting seven output-head token columns to fixed anchor columns both finish and match independently computed losses within 0.001. Training controls use assistant-only targets, data/trainer seed 0, sequential 262144-position packing and the pinned phase 0 Experiment 1 mixture. Its complete component paths, weights, reserved split and shuffle settings are in the consumed-config receipt linked below.
2. Use `XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false --xla_gpu_nccl_termination_timeout_seconds=600"` and execute the first backward/update. The local reproduction entry point is `experiments/post_training/snowball_isoflop/diagnostic.py`; source 33b69d10df preserves the isolated controls and later 97f6a242e6 exposes the explicit SFTSpec runtime field. These commits are local research commits, currently unpublished.
3. Compare the controls below, each starting from the same two-flag baseline in step 2. Baseline command-buffer and async-collective behavior is left at the JAX runtime default; neither has an extra override. Read-only inspection of a fresh campaign worker confirms jax, jaxlib, jax-cuda13-plugin and jax-cuda13-pjrt all 0.11.1. These match the GPU dependency pins used by the diagnostic source.

Expected: the first optimizer update completes, followed by finite training steps, without forced host launch synchronization.

| Runtime control | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Source async-collective runtime | First-update stall |
| Add `--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` | First-update stall; NCCL collective counts agree across all ranks (AllGather 1460, ReduceScatter 99, AllReduce 46 globally) |
| Add only `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | First-update stall |
| Add only `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=` | First-update stall |
| Both command buffers off and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | 20 finite updates, permanent step 19 checkpoint, both initial-loss gates pass |
| Source runtime under Nsight Systems CUDA/NVTX tracing | 14 finite updates before deliberate bounded termination; CUDA graphs remain active |

The successful unprofiled joint control's first update took about 99 seconds; subsequent warm inclusive median 9.2473s/update, minimum unused allocator capacity 55.54% (the JAX allocator is limited to approximately 75% of physical GPU memory). One profiled run progressed while the unprofiled source-runtime attempt stalled; repeatability of this difference is not established. Its available trace contains 1,531,280 kernels across all 8 GPUs and 91,112 cuGraphLaunch calls. The report emitted a StringStorage processing warning, so exported events have that caveat. Successful completed kernels do not identify the operation stuck in unprofiled execution. NCCL 2.31.2, CUDA runtime 13.3, driver API 13.2 were reported. Agreement of NCCL counters in the synchronous-collective control does not prove which kernel or communication operation is responsible.

Preserved profile: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/snowball-isoflop/2026.11.13.9/diagnostic-kernel-profile-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20/nsys/r00000-gb95de0.nsys-rep` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.9%2Fdiagnostic-kernel-profile-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20%2Fnsys%2Fr00000-gb95de0.nsys-rep)); exported summary is `analysis/kernel-summary.json` beside its nsys directory. Control directories in that same 2026.11.13.9 prefix are `calibration-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20` (source runtime), `diagnostic-serial-collectives-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20`, `diagnostic-launch-blocking-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20`, `diagnostic-no-command-buffer-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20`, and `diagnostic-synchronous-launches-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20`. Each preserves `consumed-config.json`, `dispatch.json` and initial-evaluation receipts. The complete successful joint-control config is [available in Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.9%2Fdiagnostic-synchronous-launches-d1024-assistant-seed0-n20%2Fconsumed-config.json). Config and profile access require Marin credentials; the local source commits are not yet a public standalone reproducer.

Exact isolated-control entry point, from the research checkout inside an 8-GPU Iris coordinator: `python -m experiments.post_training.snowball_isoflop.diagnostic --size 1024 --mask assistant --runtime synchronous-launches --h100-hour-limit 3 --run`. Replace the runtime value with `serial-collectives`, `launch-blocking` or `no-command-buffer` for the other controls. The coordinator must target cw-rno2a with interactive priority and 259200-second timeout.

Related investigations: #7110 (concurrent TVM-FFI invocation), #8870 (multi-rack ragged EP hang). This single-node CP4/data2 Sonic case has not been reduced to either mechanism.

Fresh six-cell calibration update (2026-11-14 02:51UTC): both d1024 masks with the joint runtime progressed beyond15 finite updates. All four source-runtime arms (d512 full/assistant and d768 full/assistant) passed both initial-loss gates but stalled in their first update for more than five minutes. Read-only samples of each rank main thread show ExecuteReplicated; all32GPUs report100% utilization, zero memory traffic and117–171W. The successful V9 d512/d768 assistant trajectories and these V10 stalls show that earlier small-size successes do not establish reliable source-runtime execution. The newer source adds token-count metric reductions relative to the original calibration; this is an attribution caveat, although CPU comparison verifies unchanged numerical training settings. All source-runtime failed-arm receipts remain under `2026.11.13.10/calibration-d{512,768}-{full,assistant}-seed0-n20/`; their scoped recovery uses separate `calibration-recovery-` identities.

Runtime-control update (2026-11-14 04:25UTC): command buffers off plus launch blocking completed20-update native calibrations for d768 full and both d1024 masks, but still stalled both d512 masks and d768 assistant. Adding `--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` to that joint setting completed20 finite updates for BOTH d512 masks and BOTH d768 masks, with dual initial-loss gates, finished trackers, permanent step19 checkpoints and safe allocator headroom. These are scoped loss-curve workarounds; their timings are excluded from source-runtime throughput comparisons. The corresponding SFTSpec runtime implementation is in local research source3a38e030d0 (unpublished).

A source-runtime d1024 `ring_gather_combine` control at CP4/data2 also stalled at the first update. A late CUDA-GDB attachment timed out before kernel queries; the job later failed, so retain an intervention caveat and do not infer a particular blocked kernel. Its archived output is preserved at `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/snowball-isoflop/2026.11.13.10/diagnostic-ring-r2/debugger-outputs.tar.zst` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fsnowball-isoflop%2F2026.11.13.10%2Fdiagnostic-ring-r2%2Fdebugger-outputs.tar.zst)).

A d512 assistant CP8/data1/Sonic/offload-true control using SOURCE runtime (neither extra compiler flags nor launch blocking) completed20 finite updates, both gates, permanent step19 and zero measured sender/receiver drops. Minimum allocator headroom80.19%; warm inclusive71,600 positions/s/GPU. Its supervisor recorded a rank0 cleanup segfault, although job, tracker and native checkpoint gates passed. All compared layout diagnostics use dispatch-count instrumentation, which differs from the main calibration and remains an attribution caveat. CP4/data2 offload-false was interrupted before training, so it does not establish an offload result. Geometry is a useful discriminator; a causal kernel mechanism remains unproven.

Batch-probe update (2026-11-14 04:35UTC): original SOURCE runtime also stalls d512, d768 and d1024 assistant-target CP4/data2/Sonic/offload-true probes at global batch2, microbatch1, accumulation1. All three pass both initial gates; none records an update more than9 minutes after the first batch is loaded. Read-only snapshots show all24GPUs at100% utilization and0% memory utilization, approximately118–217W. d512/d1024 main threads remain in ExecuteReplicated; d768 waits on ArrayImpl._value while reading the resulting loss scalar. Each stalled probe was stopped; total allocation6.64272H100-hours. These cells provide no valid throughput or batch-saturation measurements. Exact receipts are under `2026.11.13.10/B-accumulation-cp4-dp2-ep1-r1-sonic-offload1-mb1-acc1-grug_moe_muonh_v1-lr5e-05-d{512,768,1024}-assistant-seed0-n8/` beside the previous artifacts. This extends the observed failure beyond accumulation4/globalbatch8, without proving its cause.

The d1024 full-mask three-setting runtime (joint setting plus ALLCOLLECTIVES) also completed20 finite updates, both initial gates, finished tracking and a permanent step19 checkpoint. The matching assistant confirmation is running; uniform loss-phase runtime has not yet been selected from that pending result.

CP8 feasibility update (2026-11-14 04:59UTC): source-runtime batch8/microbatch1/accumulation8/Sonic/offload-true probes completed8 finite updates for d512 AND d768. Both have finished trackers, dual initial-loss gates, permanent step7 checkpoints and zero measured sender/receiver drops. Warm inclusive positions/s/GPU are48,324 and48,514; minimum allocator headroom81.20% and73.08%. Both supervisors killed rank0 during cleanup despite successful job/tracker/checkpoint gates. The d1024 CP8 cell passed both initial gates but stalled before its first update; two read-only samples several minutes apart show ExecuteReplicated and all8GPUs100% utilization/0% memory utilization/~118–130W. It was stopped after both smaller endpoints were verified. Thus CP8 is a positive discriminator for two sizes, not a universal recovery. All three use identical dispatch-count instrumentation and the original two E2 flags; no loss-phase runtime overrides.

The three-setting d1024 assistant confirmation also completed its first update and reached final native checkpoint/export, but its3-H100-hour bound interrupted export with only19 published training rows. It is not accepted as completed calibration and is not another first-update stall. A separate fresh4-hour confirmation preserves the interrupted artifacts and the full calibration requirements.

🤖

# Research

The compiled training step computes gradients and applies the optimizer in one execution. The reported forward evaluations and runtime controls do not identify which operation stalls. Command buffers disabled together with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` completed 20 updates; each control alone stalled. One source-runtime run under Nsight reached 14 updates, but repeatability is unknown. The cited diagnostic commits `33b69d10df` and `97f6a242e6` are absent from this checkout and GitHub; the exact workload cannot yet be reproduced from published source. [#7110](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7110) and [#8870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8870) involve different kernels or topologies and do not identify this stall.

**Relevant code**
- [`trainer.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L726-L749) — gradients and optimizer share a compiled step.
- [`snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L430-L455) — Snowball attention dispatch.
- [`_fa4_cute.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py#L311-L335) — H100 attention backend.
- [`sonic.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/sonic.py#L248-L310) — Sonic dispatch and backward.
- [`muonh.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/muonh.py#L54-L100) — Muon-H optimizer construction.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish the isolated `diagnostic.py`, its SFTSpec runtime field, and exact dependency pins in a reviewable branch. Link its consumed-config receipt. Give every trial a first-update deadline and preserve its result and source revision.
2. On the same 8×H100 configuration, repeat the source runtime and passing joint control three times each. Run a separate traced source-runtime arm to measure the Nsight effect. Record per-rank progress, NCCL RAS, XLA executable dumps, and loaded CUDA/NCCL versions; stop each stalled trial after a 10-minute first-update deadline.
3. Split the first update at the gradient/optimizer boundary with the same parameters, batch, and mesh: evaluate gradients without applying them, then apply the optimizer to captured gradients. If gradients stall, replace FA4 and Sonic independently. Capture a GPU kernel/stream stack from a stalled rank before changing more runtime flags. These ablations localize a suspect; they do not by themselves prove a cause if recompilation changes launch order.
4. Fix the identified component in Marin or report a minimal reproducer upstream. Validate the original unprofiled runtime without launch synchronization across three cold 20-update runs, with finite losses, the existing initial-loss gates, and warm-step timing against the 9.2473 s joint-control median. Add a regression test for the isolated failure before opening a fix PR.

| r6, two arms | 5e-5 / 1e-4 | EAGER, autotune level 4 | Both stalled in the first execution after compilation; stopped at the 900 s first-step rule. Zero completed updates. |
| r7, two arms | 5e-5 / 1e-4 | EAGER, autotune level 4, plus CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and ALLCOLLECTIVES | Both stalled in the first execution; stopped at the 600 s rule. Zero completed updates. |
| r5c | 2e-5 | LAZY, autotune level 0; no launch-blocking/ALLCOLLECTIVES overrides | Seven finite updates before deliberate cancellation. About 120 s/update; update-15 eval was not reached. |

The r6 deadline captures covered all 64 ranks per arm: 51 and 52 of 64, respectively, main stacks included `cuModuleLoadData → jax::cuda::TritonKernelCall`. In r7, all 64 captured main stacks in each arm instead included `cuLaunchKernelEx → ncclLaunchKernel → ncclGroupEnd → xla::gpu::NcclGroupLaunch`. Sampled GPUs showed 100% SM utilization and 0% memory utilization.

For each r7 arm, NCCL RAS samples at 07:00:49Z and 07:02:35Z on 2026-11-14 had **all 170 matched communicator/collective min/max counter entries unchanged**, with no communicators added or lost. Thus there was no observed counter advance over approximately 106 s.

The three-setting workaround reported here at 8 H100 has not qualified at our 64-H100/full-model geometry. The successful r5b run also did not establish reliability. LR constants differ across the successful and stalled cases, and the stack/counter observations do not identify a unique causal kernel. The level 0 result establishes several completed updates, not a completed held-out-eval qualification.
